1.1: And it came to be, after Alexandros son of Philippos, the Makedonian, who came out of the land of Kittim, had smitten Dareyawesh meleḵ of Paras and Maḏai, that he reigned in his place, the first over Yawan.
1.2: And he fought many battles, and won many strongholds, and slew the melaḵim of the earth.
1.3: And he went through to the ends of the earth, and took spoils from many nations, so that the earth was at rest before him; therefore he was exalted and his heart was lifted up.
1.4: And he gathered a very mighty army and ruled over countries, and nations, and melaḵim, who became tributary to him.
1.5: And after these events he fell sick, and perceived that he would die.
1.6: So he called his servants, who were honorable, and had been brought up with him from his youth, and divided his reign among them, while he was still alive.
1.7: So Alexandros reigned twelve years, and then he died.
1.8: And his servants ruled, each one in his place.
1.9: And after his death they all put crowns upon themselves, as did their sons after them many years, and evils were multiplied in the earth.
1.10: And a wicked root came out from them: Antioḵos also called Epiphanĕs, son of Antioḵos the meleḵ, who had been a hostage at Rome, and he reigned in the hundred and thirty-seventh year of the reign of the Yawanites.
1.11: In those days wicked men went out of Yisra’ĕl, who persuaded many saying, “Let us go and make a covenant with the gentiles that are round about us, for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.”
1.12: So this plan was well-pleasing to them.
1.13: Then some of the people were so bold in this, that they went to the meleḵ, who gave them authority to do according to the laws of the gentiles.
1.14: So they built a place of training at Yerushalayim according to the customs of the gentiles;
1.15: and made themselves uncircumcised, and forsook qodesh Covenant, and joined themselves to the gentiles, and were sold to do evil.
1.16: Now when the reign was established before Antioḵos, he thought to reign over Mitsrayim that he might have the rule of two reigns.
1.17: Therefore he entered into Mitsrayim with a great multitude; with chariots, and elephants, and horsemen, and a great fleet,
1.18: and fought against Ptolemaeus, meleḵ of Mitsrayim. But Ptolemaeus was afraid of him, and fled, and many were wounded and slain.
1.19: Therefore they took the fortified cities in the land of Mitsrayim and he took the spoils from there.
1.20: And after Antioḵos had smitten Mitsrayim, he returned again in the hundred and forty-third year, and went up against Yisra’ĕl and Yerushalayim with a great multitude.
1.21: And he entered proudly into the Miqdash, and took away the golden altar, and the lampstand of light, and all its utensils,
1.22: and the table of the showbread, and the bowls for pouring, and the vessels, and the gold fire holders, and the veil, and the crown, and the golden ornaments that were before Hĕyḵal, all which he pulled off.
1.23: He also took the silver and the gold, and the precious vessels. He also took the hidden treasures which he found.
1.24: And when he had taken all away, he went to his own land, having made a great slaughter, and spoken very proudly.
1.25: Therefore there was a great mourning in Yisra’ĕl, in every place where they were,
1.26: so that the rulers and elders mourned, the maidens and young men were weakened, and the pleasantness of women was changed.
1.27: Every bridegroom lamented, and she that sat in the bridal chamber was in grief.
1.28: The land also was moved for the inhabitants, and all the house of Ya’aqoḇ was covered with shame.
1.29: And after a full two years passed, the meleḵ sent his chief tax collector to the cities of Yahuḏah, who came to Yerushalayim with a great multitude,
1.30: and spoke peaceable words to them. But all was deceit, for when they had accepted him, he fell suddenly upon the city, and smote it greatly, and destroyed many people of Yisra’ĕl.
1.31: And when he had taken the spoils of the city, he lit it on fire, and pulled down the houses and its walls all around.
1.32: But they took the women and children captive, and took possession of the cattle.
1.33: Then they built the city of Dawiḏ with a great and strong wall, and with mighty towers, and made it a stronghold for themselves.
1.34: And they put a sinful nation in it - wicked men - and strengthened themselves within.
1.35: They also stored it with weapons and food, and when they had gathered together the spoils of Yerushalayim, they laid them up there. And so they became a great snare,
1.36: for it was a place to lie in wait against the Miqdash, and an evil adversary to Yisra’ĕl.
1.37: Thus they shed innocent blood on every side of the Miqdash, and defiled it,
1.38: so that the inhabitants of Yerushalayim fled because of them. Therefore the city was made a dwelling of foreigners, and became foreign to those that were born in her; and her own children left her.
1.39: Her Miqdash was laid waste like a wilderness; her Feasts were turned into mourning; her Shabbathoth into reproach; her honor into contempt.
1.40: As had been her esteem, so was her dishonor increased, and her excellency was turned into mourning.
1.41: And meleḵ Antioḵos wrote to his whole reign, that all should be one people,
1.42: and everyone should leave his laws. So all the gentiles agreed according to the command of the meleḵ.
1.43: Even many of the Yisra’ĕlites also agreed to his belief, and slaughtered to idols, and profaned the Shabbath.
1.44: For the meleḵ had sent letters by messengers to Yerushalayim and the cities of Yahuḏah that they should follow the foreign laws of the land,
1.45: and forbid burnt offerings, and slaughtering, and drink offerings, in the Hĕyḵal; and that they should profane the Shabbathoth and Festival days,
1.46: and pollute the Miqdash and qodesh people,
1.47: put up altars, and Ashĕrim, and temples of idols, and offer pig’s flesh, and unclean beasts.
1.48: That they should also leave their children uncircumcised, and make their beings abominable with all manner of uncleanness and abomination,
1.49: so that they might forget the Torah, and change all the Laws.
1.50: And whoever would not do according to the command of the meleḵ, he said, “He should die.”
1.51: He wrote to his whole reign in the same way, and appointed overseers over all the people, commanding the cities of Yahuḏah to offer, city by city.
1.52: Then many of the people were gathered to them, that is, every one that forsook the Torah; and so they committed evils in the land,
1.53: and drove the Yisra’ĕlites into hiding places, even wherever they could flee for safety.
1.54: Now on the fifteenth day of the month Kislĕw, in the hundred and forty-fifth year, they put up the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and built idol altars throughout the cities of Yahuḏah on every side,
1.55: and burned incense at the doors of their houses, and in the streets.
1.56: And when they had torn in pieces the Books of the Torah which they found, they burned them with fire.
1.57: And whoever was found with any of the Book of the Covenant, or if any adhered to the Torah, the meleḵ’s command was that they should put him to death.
1.58: Thus they did by their authority to the Yisra’ĕlites every month, to as many as were found in the cities.
1.59: Now on the twenty-fifth day of the month they slaughtered on the idol altar, which was upon the altar of Elohim,
1.60: at which time, according to the command they put to death some women that had allowed their children to be circumcised.
1.61: And they hanged the infants by their necks, and ransacked their houses, and slew those that had circumcised them.
1.62: However, many in Yisra’ĕl were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean matter.
1.63: Therefore rather to die, that they might not be defiled with food, and that they might not profane the qodesh Covenant; so then they died.
1.64: And very great wrath came to be upon Yisra’ĕl.

10.1: In the hundred and sixtieth year, Alexandros the son of Antioḵos, also named Epiphanĕs, went up and took Ptolemais; for the people had received him, by means of which he reigned there.
10.2: Now when Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios heard of this, he gathered together an exceedingly great army, and went out to fight against him.
10.3: And Dĕmĕtrios sent letters to Yahonathan with kind words, so that he exalted him.
10.4: For said he, “Let us first make peace with him, before he joins with Alexandros against us,
10.5: or else he will remember all the evils that we have done against him, and against his brothers and his people.”
10.6: Therefore he gave him authority to gather together an army, and to provide weapons, that he might aid him in battle. He also commanded that the hostages that were in the tower should be delivered to him.
10.7: Then Yahonathan came to Yerushalayim and read the letters in the hearing of all the people and of those that were in the tower,
10.8: who were greatly afraid when they heard that the meleḵ had given him authority to gather together an army.
10.9: So those of the tower delivered their hostages to Yahonathan, and delivered them to their parents.
10.10: This done, Yahonathan settled himself in Yerushalayim, and began to build and repair the city.
10.11: And he commanded the workmen to build the walls and Mount Tsiyon round about with square stones for fortification; and they did so.
10.12: Then the foreigners, that were in the fortresses which Bakḵidĕs had built, fled away;
10.13: so that every man left his place and went into his own land.
10.14: Only, some of those still remained at Bĕyth Tsur that had forsaken the Torah and the Commands; for it was their place of refuge.
10.15: Now when Meleḵ Alexandros had heard what promises Dĕmĕtrios had sent to Yahonathan; when it was also told to him of the battles and brave deeds which he and his brothers had done, and of the pains that they had endured,
10.16: He said, “Shall we find such another man? Now therefore we will make him our friend and ally.”
10.17: Therefore he wrote a letter, and sent it to him, according to these words, saying:
10.18: “Meleḵ Alexandros, to his brother Yahonathan, greetings.
10.19: “We have heard of you, that you are a man of great strength, and worthy to be our friend.
10.20: “Therefore now, we ordain you this day to be the kohĕn ha’gadol of your nation, and to be called the meleḵ’s friend, and require you to take our side, and maintain friendship with us.” And with all this he sent him a purple robe and a crown of gold.
10.21: So in the seventh month of the hundred and sixtieth year, at the Feast of Sukkoth, Yahonathan put on the qodesh robe, and gathered together forces, and provided much armor.
10.22: When Dĕmĕtrios heard of this, he was very grieved, and said,
10.23: “What have we done, that Alexandros has prevented us in making peace with the Yahuḏim to strengthen himself?
10.24: “I will also write words of encouragement to them, and promise them esteem and gifts, that I may have their support.”
10.25: Therefore he sent to them to this word: “Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios, to the people of the Yahuḏim, greetings.
10.26: “Whereas you have kept covenants with us, and continued in our friendship, not joining yourselves with our enemies, we have heard of this, and are glad.
10.27: “Therefore now continue to be still trustworthy to us, and we will recompense you well for the matters you do on our behalf,
10.28: and will grant you many exemptions, and give you rewards.
10.29: “And I now release you, and for your sake, I release all the Yahuḏim from tributes, and from the customs of salt, and from crown taxes,
10.30: and from that which pertains to me to receive of the third part of the seed, and the half of the fruit of the trees. I release it from this day onward, so that they shall not be taken from the land of Yahuḏah, nor of the three governments which are added to them out of the country of Shomeron and Galil, from this day onward, forever.
10.31: “Let Yerushalayim also be qodesh and released, with its borders, both from tenths and tributes.
10.32: “And as for the tower which is at Yerushalayim, I yield up authority over it, and give to the kohĕn ha’gadol, that he may appoint in it such men as he shall choose to guard it.
10.33: “And I freely release every one of the Yahuḏim, that were carried captive out of the land of Yahuḏah into any part of my reign, and I purpose that all my officers release the tributes even of their cattle.
10.34: “Furthermore, I purpose that all the Feasts, and Shabbathoth, and New Moons, and Appointed Times, and the three days before the Feast, and the three days after the Feast shall be all of tolerance and freedom for all the Yahuḏim in my reign.
10.35: “Also, no man shall have authority to meddle with or to provoke any of them in any matter.
10.36: “I further purpose, that there be enrolled among the meleḵ’s forces about thirty thousand men of the Yahuḏim, to whom wages shall be given, as belongs to all meleḵ’s forces.
10.37: “And of them, some shall be positioned in the meleḵ’s strongholds, some of whom are trustworthy shall also be appointed over the affairs of the reign. And I purpose that their overseers and governors be from among themselves, and that they live after their own Laws, even as the meleḵ has commanded in the land of Yahuḏah.
10.38: “And concerning the three governments that are added to Yahuḏah from the country of Shomeron, let them be joined with Yahuḏah, that they may be reckoned to be under one, nor bound to obey authority other than the kohĕn ha’gadol.
10.39: “As for Ptolemais, and the land pertaining to it, I give it as a free gift to the Miqdash at Yerushalayim for the necessary expenses of the Miqdash.
10.40: “And every year I give fifteen thousand shekels of silver out of the meleḵ’s accounts from the pertaining places,
10.41: and all the remainder, which the officers did not pay as in former time, from now on shall be given toward the works of the Hĕyḵal.
10.42: “And besides this, the five thousand shekels of silver which they took from the uses of the Hĕyḵal out of the accounts year by year, even those shall be released, because they pertain to the kohenim that serve.
10.43: “And whoever flees to the Hĕyḵal at Yerushalayim, or comes within these freedoms, being indebted to the meleḵ, or for any other matter, let them be released, and all that they have in my reign.
10.44: “Also for the building and repairing of the works of the Miqdash, expenses shall be given from the meleḵ’s accounts.
10.45: “And also for the building of the walls of Yerushalayim, and its fortifications round about, expenses shall be given out of the meleḵ’s accounts, as also for the building of the walls in Yahuḏah.”
10.46: Now when Yahonathan and the people heard these words, they gave them no trust, nor received them, because they remembered the great evil that he had done in Yisra’ĕl; for he had afflicted them very greatly.
10.47: But with Alexandros they were well pleased, because he was the first that sought true peace with them, and they were allied with him always.
10.48: Then Meleḵ Alexandros gathered great forces, and encamped opposite Dĕmĕtrios.
10.49: And after the two melaḵim had joined battle, Dĕmĕtrios’ army fled, but Alexandros followed after him, and prevailed against them.
10.50: And he continued the battle greatly until the sun went down; and Dĕmĕtrios was slain that day.
10.51: Afterward, Alexandros sent ambassadors to Ptolemaeus meleḵ of Mitsrayim with a message to this effect:
10.52: “Since I have come again to my reign, and am appointed to the throne of my ancestors, and have acquired the reign, and overthrown Dĕmĕtrios, and recovered our country;
10.53: for after I had joined battle with him, both he and his army were defeated by us, so that we sit on the throne of his reign.
10.54: Now therefore let us make a covenant of peace together, and give me now your daughter as wife, and I will be your son-in-law, and will give both to you and her according to your dignity.”
10.55: Then Ptolemaeus the meleḵ gave answer, saying, “Joyful is the day in which you returned to the land of your fathers, and sat on the throne of their reign.
10.56: “And now I will do to you, as you have written. Therefore meet me at Ptolemais, that we may see one another; for I will marry my daughter to you according to your desire.”
10.57: So Ptolemaeus went out of Mitsrayim with his daughter Cleopatra, and they came to Ptolemais in the hundred and sixty-second year,
10.58: where Meleḵ Alexandros met him, gave to him his daughter Cleopatra, and celebrated her marriage at Ptolemais with great esteem, as is the manner of melaḵim.
10.59: Now Meleḵ Alexandros had written to Yahonathan, that he should come and meet him,
10.60: who therefore went honorably to Ptolemais, where he met the two melaḵim, and gave they and their friends silver and gold and many gifts, and found favor in their sight.
10.61: At that time some wicked men of Yisra’ĕl, men of a Beliya’al, assembled themselves against him to accuse him; but the meleḵ would not hear them.
10.62: Yet furthermore, the meleḵ commanded to take off his garments, and clothe him in purple; and they did so.
10.63: And he made him sit beside him, and said to his princes, “Go with him into the midst of the city, and proclaim, that no man complain against him for any matter, and that no man trouble him for any reason.”
10.64: Now when his accusers saw that he was honored according to the proclamation, and clothed in purple, they all fled.
10.65: So the meleḵ honored him, and wrote him among his chief friends, and made him a chief, and shared in his reign.
10.66: Afterward, Yahonathan returned to Yerushalayim in peace and gladness.
10.67: Furthermore, in the hundred and sixty-fifth year Dĕmĕtrios son of Dĕmĕtrios came out of Krĕtĕ into the land of his fathers.
10.68: When Meleḵ Alexandros heard of this, he was grieved, and returned to Antioḵeia.
10.69: Then Dĕmĕtrios made Apollonios the governor of Koĕlĕ Suria his general, who gathered together a great army, and encamped in Yaḇneh, and sent to Yahonathan the kohĕn ha’gadol saying,
10.70: “You alone lift yourself up against us, and I am mocked for your sake and reproached, and why do you boast of your strength against us in the mountains?
10.71: “Now therefore, if you trust in your own strength, come down to us into the field of the plains, and there let us try the matter together. For the strength of the cities is with me.
10.72: “Ask, and learn who I am, and the rest that take our side, and they shall tell you that your foot is not able to flee in their own land.
10.73: “Therefore now, you shall not be able to stand against the horsemen and such a great strength in the plain, where there is neither stone nor flint, nor a place to flee to!”
10.74: So when Yahonathan heard these words of Apollonios, he was moved in his mind, and choosing ten thousand men he went out of Yerushalayim, where Shim’on his brother met him to help him.
10.75: And he pitched his tents against Yapho, but those of Yapho shut him out of the city, because Apollonios had a garrison there.
10.76: Then Yahonathan laid siege against it, so those of the city let him in for fear. And so Yahonathan won Yapho.
10.77: When Apollonios heard of this, he took three thousand horsemen, with a great army of footmen, and went to Ashdoḏ as one that journeyed, and then approached the plain, because he had a great number of horsemen, in whom he put his trust.
10.78: Then Yahonathan followed after him to Ashdoḏ where the armies joined battle.
10.79: Now Apollonios had left one thousand horsemen in ambush.
10.80: And Yahonathan knew that there was an ambush behind him; for they had surrounded his army, and shot arrows at the people, from morning till evening.
10.81: But the people stood still, as Yahonathan had commanded them, and so the enemy’s horses were tired.
10.82: Then brought Shim’on out his army, and positioned them against the footmen, for the horsemen who were defeated by him were weary, and fled.
10.83: The horsemen also, being scattered in the field, fled to Ashdoḏ, and went to the house of Daḡon, their idol’s temple, for safety.
10.84: But Yahonathan lit fire to Ashdoḏ, and the cities round about it, and took their spoils. And he burned the temple of Daḡon with fire with those that had fled into it,
10.85: so there were nearly eight thousand men burned and slain with the sword.
10.86: And from there Yahonathan moved his army, and encamped against Ashqelon, where the men of the city came out and met him with great ceremony.
10.87: After this, Yahonathan and his army returned to Yerushalayim possessing many spoils.
10.88: Now, when Meleḵ Alexandros heard these matters, he honored Yahonathan still further,
10.89: and sent him a gold buckle, as is the custom to be given to those of the meleḵ’s blood. He also gave him Eqron with its borders as a possession.

11.1: And the meleḵ of Mitsrayim gathered together a great army, like the sand that lies upon the sea shore, and many ships, and through deceit attempted to gain the reign of Alexandros, and join it to his own.
11.2: So he departed to Spania in a peaceable manner, so that those of the cities opened to him, and met him; for Meleḵ Alexandros had commanded them to do so, because he was his brother-in-law.
11.3: Now as Ptolemaeus entered into the cities, he positioned a garrison of soldiers in every one of them to guard it.
11.4: And when he came near to Ashdoḏ, they showed him the temple of Daḡon that was burned, and Ashdoḏ and the suburbs of there that were destroyed, and the bodies that were thrown about and those that he had burned in the battle; for they had made heaps of them by the way where he should pass.
11.5: They also told the meleḵ all Yahonathan had done, to the intent he might blame him, but the meleḵ held his peace.
11.6: Then Yahonathan met the meleḵ with great ceremony at Yapho, where they greeted one another, and stayed.
11.7: Afterward, when Yahonathan had gone with the meleḵ to the river called Eleutherus, he returned again to Yerushalayim.
11.8: Therefore Meleḵ Ptolemaeus, having gained the reign of the cities by the sea to Seleukeia on the sea coast, devised wicked plans against Alexandros.
11.9: So he sent ambassadors to Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios, saying, “Come, let us make an alliance between us, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexandros has, and you shall reign in your father’s reign.
11.10: “For I regret that I gave my daughter to him, for he sought to slay me.”
11.11: So he slandered him, because he desired his reign.
11.12: Therefore he took his daughter from him, and gave her to Dĕmĕtrios, and forsook Alexandros, so that their hatred was openly known.
11.13: Then Ptolemaeus came to Antioḵeia, where he placed two crowns upon his head: the crown of Asia, and of Mitsrayim.
11.14: In the winter, Meleḵ Alexandros was in Kilikia, because those that dwelt in those parts had revolted against him.
11.15: But when Alexandros heard of this, he came to fight against him; so Meleḵ Ptolemaeus brought forth his army, and met him with a mighty strength, and put him to flight.
11.16: So Alexandros fled to Araḇia to take defense there, but Meleḵ Ptolemaeus was exalted.
11.17: For Zaḇdi’ĕl the Araḇian took off Alexandros’ head, and sent it to Ptolemaeus.
11.18: Meleḵ Ptolemaeus also died after the third day, and those that were in the strongholds were slain, one after another.
11.19: Because of this, Dĕmĕtrios reigned in the hundred and sixty-seventh year.
11.20: At the same time Yahonathan gathered together those that were in Yahuḏah to take the tower that was in Yerushalayim, and he built many siege engines against it.
11.21: Then wicked men, who hated their own people, went to the meleḵ, and told him that Yahonathan besieged the tower.
11.22: When he heard of this, he was wroth, and moving immediately, he came to Ptolemais and wrote to Yahonathan, that he should not lay siege to the tower, but come quickly and speak with him at Ptolemais.
11.23: Nevertheless, when Yahonathan heard this, he commanded to continue the siege, and he chose some of the elders of Yisra’ĕl and the kohenim, and put himself at risk,
11.24: and took silver and gold and garments, and also various presents, and went to Ptolemais to the meleḵ, where he found favor in his sight.
11.25: And though some wicked men of the people had made complaints against him,
11.26: the meleḵ still treated him as his predecessors had done before, and promoted him in the sight of all his friends,
11.27: and confirmed him in the high kehunnah, and in all the honors that he had before, and made him first among his chief friends.
11.28: Then Yahonathan requested from the meleḵ, that he would make Yahuḏah free from tribute, as also the three governments, with the country of Shomeron; and he promised him three hundred talanton.
11.29: So the meleḵ agreed, and wrote letters for Yahonathan of all these matters after this manner:
11.30: “Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios to his brother Yahonathan, and to the nation of the Yahuḏim, greetings.
11.31: “We send you here a copy of the letter which we wrote to our cousin Lasthĕnĕs concerning you, that you might see it.
11.32: ‘Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios to his father Lasthĕnĕss sends greeting.
11.33: “We are determined to do good to the people of the Yahuḏim, who are our friends, and guard covenants with us, because of their favor toward us.
11.34: ‘Therefore we have assigned to them the borders of Yahuḏah, with the three governments of Ephrayim and Loḏ and Ramathayim, that are added to Yahuḏah from the country of Shomeron, and all pertaining to them, for all those who offer in Yerushalayim, instead of the payments which the meleḵ received from them yearly previously out of the fruits of the earth and of trees.
11.35: ‘And as for other matters that relate to us, of the tithes and customs pertaining to us, and also the salt-pits and the crown taxes which are due to us, we release them all for their aid.
11.36: ‘And none of this shall be revoked from this time on forever.
11.37: ‘Now therefore, see that you make a copy of these matters, and let it be delivered to Yahonathan, and put on the qodesh mountain in a conspicuous place.’ ”
11.38: After this, when Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios saw that the land was at peace before him, and that no resistance was made against him, he sent away all his armies, every one to his own place, except some bands of foreigners, whom he had gathered from the islands of the gentiles; therefore all the armies of his fathers hated him.
11.39: Now there was one Truphon, that had been of Alexandros’ group before, who, seeing that all the army grumbled against Dĕmĕtrios, went to Imalkuĕ the Araḇian that brought up Antioḵos the young son of Alexandros,
11.40: and pressured him to deliver him this young Antioḵos, that he might reign in his father’s place. So he told him of all that Dĕmĕtrios had done, and how his soldiers were at enmity with him, and he remained there a long time.
11.41: In the meantime, Yahonathan sent to Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios, that he would throw those of the tower out of Yerushalayim, and also those in the fortresses; for they fought against Yisra’ĕl.
11.42: So Dĕmĕtrios sent to Yahonathan saying, “I will not only do this for you and your people, but I will greatly honor you and your nation, if opportunity arises.
11.43: “Now therefore you shall do well if you send me men to help me; for all my forces are gone from me.”
11.44: Upon this Yahonathan sent him three thousand strong men to Antioḵeia; and when they came to the meleḵ, the meleḵ was very glad of their arrival.
11.45: However those that were from the city gathered themselves together into the midst of the city, numbering a hundred and twenty thousand men, and would have slain the meleḵ.
11.46: So the meleḵ fled into the court, but those of the city guarded the passages of the city, and began to fight.
11.47: Then the meleḵ called to the Yahuḏim for help, who came to him all at once, and dispersing themselves throughout the city slew that day in the city to the number of a hundred thousand.
11.48: They also lit the city on fire, and gathered many spoils that day, and delivered the meleḵ.
11.49: So when those of the city saw that the Yahuḏim had taken the city as they would, their courage decreased, therefore they made supplication to the meleḵ, and cried, saying,
11.50: “Grant us peace, and let the Yahuḏim cease from assaulting us and the city!”
11.51: With that, they threw down their weapons, and made peace; and the Yahuḏim were honored in the sight of the meleḵ and in the sight of all that were in his reign; and they returned to Yerushalayim, having great spoils.
11.52: So Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios sat on the throne of his reign, and the land was at rest before him.
11.53: However, he deceived in all that he spoke, and estranged himself from Yahonathan, neither rewarded him according to the good which he had received from him, but troubled him deeply.
11.54: After this, Truphon returned, and the young child Antioḵos with him, who was crowned and reigned.
11.55: Then all the men of battle gathered to him, whom Dĕmĕtrios had put away, and they fought against Dĕmĕtrios, who turned his back and fled.
11.56: Then Truphon took the elephants, and won Antioḵeia.
11.57: At that time young Antioḵos wrote to Yahonathan, saying, “I confirm you in the high kehunnah and appoint you ruler over the four governments and to be one of the meleḵ’s friends.”
11.58: Then he sent him golden vessels to be served in, allowed him to drink in gold, and to be clothed in purple, and to wear a golden buckle.
11.59: He also made Shim’on his brother captain of the place called ‘The ladder of Tsor’ to the borders of Mitsrayim.
11.60: Then Yahonathan went out, and passed through the cities beyond the waters, and all the forces of Suria gathered themselves to him to assist him. And when he came to Ashqelon, those of the city met him honorably.
11.61: From there he went to Azzah, but those of Azzah shut him out, so he laid siege to it, and burned the open lands with fire, and plundered them.
11.62: Afterward, when those of Azzah made supplication to Yahonathan, he made peace with them, and took the sons of their chief men for hostages, and sent them to Yerushalayim, and passed through the country to Dammeseq.
11.63: Now when Yahonathan heard that the princes of Dĕmĕtrios had come to Qaḏĕsh, which is in Galil, with a great force, with the purpose of removing him out of the land,
11.64: he went to meet them, and left Shim’on his brother in the land.
11.65: Then Shim’on encamped against Bĕyth Tsur and fought against it a long time, and shut it up.
11.66: But they desired for peace with him, which he granted them, and then put them out from there, and took the city, and positioned a garrison in it.
11.67: As for Yahonathan and his army, they encamped at the lake of Gennĕsar, and early in the morning they went from there to the plain of Ḥatsor.
11.68: And see, the army of foreigners met them in the plain, who, having laid men in ambush for him in the mountains, they came opposite him.
11.69: So when those that lay in ambush rose out of their places and joined battle, all that were of Yahonathan’s side fled;
11.70: so that there was not one of them left, except Mattithyahu the son of Aḇshalom, and Yahuḏah the son of Ḥalphi, the captains of the army.
11.71: Then Yahonathan tore his garments, and threw dust upon his head, and prayed.
11.72: After turning again to battle, he put them to flight, and so they ran away.
11.73: Now when his own men that had fled saw this, they turned again toward him, and with him, pursued them to Qaḏĕsh, even to their own tents, and there they encamped.
11.74: So there were slain that day about three thousand men of the gentiles, but Yahonathan returned to Yerushalayim.

12.1: Now when Yahonathan saw that time served him, he chose some men, and sent them to Rome, to confirm and renew the alliance that they had with them.
12.2: He also sent letters to the Lakedaemonians, and to other places, for the same purpose.
12.3: So they went to Rome, and entered into the senate, and said, “Yahonathan the kohĕn ha’gadol, and the people of the Yahuḏim, sent us to you, so that you should renew the friendship which you had with them, and alliance as before.”
12.4: Upon this, the Romans gave them letters to the governors of every place that they should bring them into the land of Yahuḏah peaceably.
12.5: And this is the copy of the letters which Yahonathan wrote to the Lakedaemonians:
12.6: “Yahonathan the kohĕn ha’gadol, and the elders of the nation, and the kohenim, and the other of the Yahuḏim, to the Lakedaemonians their brothers, greetings.
12.7: “There were letters sent in time past to Onyah the kohĕn ha’gadol from Dareyawesh, who then reigned among you, to signify that you are our brothers, as the copy here underwritten specifies;
12.8: at which time Onyah entreated the ambassador that was sent honorably, and received the letters, in which declaration was made of the alliance and friendship.
12.9: “Therefore we also - although we need none of these matters, in that we have the qodesh Books of Scripture in our hands to comfort us -
12.10: have nevertheless attempted to send to you for the renewing of brotherhood and friendship, lest we should become strangers to you altogether; for a long time has passed since you sent to us.
12.11: “We therefore at all times without ceasing, both in our Feasts, and other convenient days, remember you in the slaughterings which we offer, and in our prayers, as is right, and as it is fitting for us to think upon our brothers,
12.12: and we are rightly pleased for your honor.
12.13: “As for ourselves, we have had great troubles and battles on every side, because the melaḵim that are round about us have fought against us.
12.14: “However, we would not be troublesome to you, nor to others of our allies and friends, in these battles,
12.15: for we have help from the shamayim that upholds us, so that we are delivered from our enemies, and our enemies are brought under foot.
12.16: “For this cause we chose Numĕnios the son of Antioḵos, and Antipater the son of Yason, and sent them to the Romans, to renew the friendship that we had with them, and the former alliance.
12.17: “We also commanded them to go to you, and to greet and to deliver you our letters concerning the renewing of our brotherhood.
12.18: “Therefore now you shall do well to give us an answer to this.”
12.19: And this is the copy of the letters which he sent to Onyah:
12.20: “Arĕios meleḵ of the Lakedaemonians to Onyah the kohĕn ha’gadol; greetings.
12.21: “It is found in writing, that the Lakedaemonians and Yahuḏim are brothers, and that they are of the race of Aḇraham.
12.22: “Now therefore, since this has come to our knowledge, you shall do well to write to us of your prosperity.
12.23: “We write back again to you, that your cattle and goods are ours, and ours are yours. We command therefore our ambassadors to make report to you in this way.”
12.24: Now when Yahonathan heard that Dĕmĕtrios’ princes had come to fight against him with a greater army than before,
12.25: he moved from Yerushalayim, and met them in the land of Amathos; for he gave them no release to enter his country.
12.26: He also sent spies to their tents, who came again, and told him that they were positioned to attack them in the night.
12.27: Therefore, as soon as the sun was down, Yahonathan commanded his men to be armed and to watch all night long so that they would be ready to fight. He also sent out watchmen round about the army.
12.28: But when the adversaries heard that Yahonathan and his men were ready for battle, they feared, and trembled in their hearts, and they kindled fires in their camp.
12.29: However Yahonathan and his army did not know it till the morning; for they saw the lights burning.
12.30: Then Yahonathan pursued after them, but did not overtake them, for they had passed over the River Eleutherus.
12.31: Therefore Yahonathan turned to the Araḇians, who were called Zaḇaḏeans, and smote them, and took their spoils.
12.32: And moving from there, he came to Dammeseq, and so passed through all the land.
12.33: Shim’on also went out and passed through the land to Ashqelon and the towers beside there, from where he turned aside to Yapho, and took it,
12.34: for he had heard that they would deliver the stronghold to those that allied with Dĕmĕtrios; therefore he positioned a garrison there to guard it.
12.35: After this, Yahonathan returned home again, and calling the elders of the people together, he consulted with them about building strongholds in Yahuḏah,
12.36: and making the walls of Yerushalayim higher, and raising a great mound between the tower and the city to separate it from the city, so that it might stand alone, that men might neither sell nor buy in it.
12.37: Upon this they came together to build up the city, because part of the wall toward the wadi on the east side had fallen down, and they repaired that which was called Kaphenatha.
12.38: Shim’on also built up Aḏiḏa in Shephelah, and strengthened if with gates and bars.
12.39: Now Truphon went about to take the reign of Asia, and to kill Antioḵos the meleḵ, that he might place the crown upon his own head.
12.40: However he was afraid that Yahonathan would not allow him, and that he would fight against him; therefore he sought a way how to take Yahonathan, that he might kill him. So he moved, and came to Bĕyth She’an.
12.41: Then Yahonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for the battle, and came to Bĕyth She’an.
12.42: Now when Truphon saw Yahonathan come with so great a force, he dared not stretch out his hand against him;
12.43: but received him honorably, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his men of battle to be as obedient to him, as to himself.
12.44: To Yahonathan he also said, “Why have you brought all this people such great trouble, seeing there is no battle between us?
12.45: “Now therefore, send them home again, and choose a few men to wait on you, and you, come with me to Ptolemais, for I will give it to you, and the rest of the strongholds and forces, and all that have any charge. As for me, I will return and depart, for this is why I have come.”
12.46: So Yahonathan believing him, did as he asked him, and sent away his army, who went into the land of Yahuḏah.
12.47: And he only kept three thousand men with himself, of which he sent two thousand into Galil, and one thousand went with him.
12.48: Now as soon as Yahonathan entered into Ptolemais, those of Ptolemais shut the gates and took him, and all those that came with him they slew with the sword.
12.49: Then Truphon sent an army of footmen and horsemen into Galil, and into the great plain to destroy all Yahonathan’s army.
12.50: But when they knew that Yahonathan and those that were with him were taken and slain, they encouraged one another, and drew close together preparing to fight.
12.51: Therefore those that pursued them, seeing that they were ready to fight for their lives, turned back again.
12.52: So they all came into the land of Yahuḏah peaceably, and there they mourned for Yahonathan, and those that were with him, and they were very afraid. And so all Yisra’ĕl made a great lamentation.
12.53: Then all the gentiles that were round about sought to destroy them, for they said, “They have no captain, nor any to help them. Now therefore let us fight them, and take away their remembrance from among men.”

13.1: Now when Shim’on heard that Truphon had gathered together a great army to invade the land of Yahuḏah, and destroy it,
13.2: and seeing that the people were in great trembling and fear, went up to Yerushalayim, and gathered the people together,
13.3: and gave them encouragement, saying, “You yourselves know what great deeds my brothers and I and my father’s house have done for the Laws and the Miqdash; also the battles and troubles which we have seen.
13.4: “For this reason all my brothers are slain for Yisra’ĕl’s sake, and I alone am left.
13.5: “Now therefore, far be it from me that I should spare my own life in any time of trouble, for I am no better than my brothers.
13.6: “Certainly I shall avenge my nation, and the Miqdash and our wives and our children; for all the gentiles are gathered with great evil to destroy us.”
13.7: Now as soon as the people heard these words their spirit revived,
13.8: and they answered with a loud voice saying, “You shall be our leader instead of Yahuḏah and Yahonathan your brother!”
13.9: “You fight our battles, and whatever, you command us, that we shall do.”
13.10: So then he gathered together all the men of battle, and made haste to finish the walls of Yerushalayim, and he fortified it round about.
13.11: He also sent Yahonathan the son of Aḇshalom, and a great force with him to Yapho, who throwing out those that were there, remained there in it.
13.12: So Truphon moved from Ptolemais with a great strength to invade the land of Yahuḏah, and Yahonathan was with him under guard.
13.13: But Shim’on pitched his tents at Aḏiḏa, opposite the plain.
13.14: Now when Truphon knew that Shim’on had risen up instead of his brother Yahonathan, and meant to fight with him, he sent messengers to him, saying,
13.15: “Although we have Yahonathan your brother under guard, it is for silver that he owes to the meleḵ’s treasury, concerning that which was delivered to him.
13.16: “Now therefore, send a hundred talanton of silver and two of his sons as hostages, that when he is released he may not revolt against us, and we will let him go.”
13.17: Although Shim’on perceived that they spoke deceitfully to him, because of this he sent the silver and the children, lest he should possibly gain great hatred for himself from the people,
13.18: who might have said, “Because he did not send him the silver and the children, therefore Yahonathan is dead.”
13.19: So he sent them the children and the hundred talanton. However, Truphon was deceitful, neither would he let Yahonathan go.
13.20: And after this, Truphon came to invade the land and destroy it, going round about by the way that leads to Aḏorayim. But Shim’on and his army marched against him in every place, wherever he went.
13.21: Now those that were in the tower sent messengers to Truphon, so that he should hasten his coming to them by the wilderness, and send them food.
13.22: Therefore Truphon prepared all his horsemen to come that night, but he did not come because a very great snow fell. So he departed, and came into the land of Gil’aḏ.
13.23: And when he came near to Baskama he slew Yahonathan, who was buried there.
13.24: Afterward Truphon returned and went into his own land.
13.25: Then Shim’on sent, and took the bones of Yahonathan his brother, and buried them in Modi’im, the city of his fathers,
13.26: and all Yisra’ĕl made a great lamentation for him, and mourned for him many days.
13.27: Shim’on also built a monument upon the tomb of his father and his brothers, and raised it up to be seen, with hewn stone in front and behind.
13.28: And, he put up seven memorials, one against another, for his father, and his mother, and his four brothers.
13.29: And in these he made skilled works, around which he placed great column. And he placed all their armor upon the columns for a remembrance forever, and ships were carved by the armor, that they might be seen of all that sail on the sea.
13.30: This is the tomb which he made at Modi’im, and it still stands to this day.
13.31: Now Truphon dealt deceitfully with the young Meleḵ Antioḵos, and slew him,
13.32: and he reigned in his place, and crowned himself meleḵ of Asia, and brought great distress upon the land.
13.33: Then Shim’on built up the strongholds in Yahuḏah, and walled them around with high towers, and great walls, and gates, and bars, and stored up food within.
13.34: And Shim’on chose men, and sent to Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios so that he would give the land immunity, because all that Truphon did was to plunder;
13.35: unto whom Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios answered and wrote after this manner:
13.36: “Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios, to Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol, and friend of melaḵim, also to the elders and nation of the Yahuḏim, greetings.
13.37: “The golden crown, and the scarlet robe which you sent to us, we have received, and we are ready to make lasting peace with you, and also to write to our officers to confirm the immunities which we have granted.
13.38: “And whatever covenants we have made with you shall stand, and the strongholds which you have built shall be your own.
13.39: “As for any oversight or fault committed to this day, we forgive it, and also the crown tax which you owe us. And if there were any other tribute paid in Yerushalayim, it shall no longer be paid.
13.40: “And seek those who are upright among you to be in our court; let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.”
13.41: Thus the yoke of the gentiles was taken away from Yisra’ĕl in the hundred and seventieth year.
13.42: Then the people of Yisra’ĕl began to write in their documents and contracts, “In the first year of Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol, the governor and leader of the Yahuḏim.”
13.43: In those days Shim’on encamped against Azzah and besieged it round about. He also made a siege engine, and positioned it by the city, and battered a certain tower, and took it.
13.44: And those that were in the siege engine leaped into the city; therefore there was such a great uproar in the city,
13.45: that the people of the city tore their garments, and climbed up on the walls with their wives and children, and cried with a loud voice pleading for Shim’on to grant them peace.
13.46: And they said, “Do not deal with us according to our wickedness, but according to your kindness!”
13.47: So Shim’on was appeased toward them and no longer fought against them, but put them out of the city, and cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and so entered into it as he sang praise and baraḵ.
13.48: He also removed all its uncleanness, and appointed men there that would guard the Torah, and made it stronger than it was before, and built a dwelling place for himself there.
13.49: Also, those of the tower in Yerushalayim were kept so restricted, that they could neither come out, nor go into the country, nor buy, nor sell. Therefore they were in great distress for need of food, and a great number of them perished through scarcity of food.
13.50: Then they cried to Shim’on, pleading for him to be at one with them, which he granted them. And when he had put them out from there, he cleansed the tower from uncleannesses,
13.51: and entered into it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the hundred and seventy-first year with thanksgiving and branches of palm trees, and with harps and cymbals and with stringed instruments, and songs of praise and songs; because a great enemy was destroyed out of Yisra’ĕl.
13.52: He also ordained that the day should be kept every year with gladness. And he made the hill of the Hĕyḵal that was by the tower stronger than it was, and he dwelt there himself with his army.
13.53: And when Shim’on saw that Yoḥanan his son was a brave man, he made him captain of all the armies; and he dwelt in Gezer.

14.1: Now in the hundred and seventy-second year Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios gathered his forces together, and went into Maḏai to gain help to fight against Truphon.
14.2: But when Arsakĕs, the meleḵ of Paras and Maḏai, heard that Dĕmĕtrios had entered within his borders, he sent one of his princes to take him alive,
14.3: who went and smote the army of Dĕmĕtrios, and took him and brought him to Arsakĕs, by whom he was put under guard.
14.4: As for the land of Yahuḏah, it was quiet all the days of Shim’on; for he sought the good of his nation in order that his authority and honor pleased them well all the days.
14.5: And as he was honorable in all his deeds, so in this, that he took Yapho for a harbor, and made an entrance to the islands of the sea,
14.6: and enlarged the boundary of his nation, and recovered the land,
14.7: and gathered together a great number of captives, and had the reign of Gezer, and Bĕyth Tsur, and the tower, out of the which he took all uncleanness, neither was there any that resisted him.
14.8: Then they tilled their ground in peace, and the earth gave its increase, and the trees of the field their fruit.
14.9: All the old men sat in the streets, speaking good words together, and the young men put on splendid armor.
14.10: He provided food for the cities, and appointed in them all manner of fortification, so that his honorable name was known to the ends of the world.
14.11: He made peace in the land, and Yisra’ĕl rejoiced with great joy,
14.12: for every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to trouble them,
14.13: neither was there any left in the land to fight against them. The melaḵim themselves were also overthrown in those days,
14.14: and he strengthened all those of his people that were brought low. He searched out the Torah, and he removed every despiser of the Torah and wicked person.
14.15: He adorned the Miqdash, and multiplied vessels for the Hĕyḵal.
14.16: Now when it was heard in Rome, and as far as Sparta, that Yahonathan was dead, they were very sorry,
14.17: but as soon as they heard that his brother Shim’on was made kohĕn ha’gadol in his place, and ruled the country, and the cities there,
14.18: they wrote to him on tablets of bronze, to renew the friendship and alliance which they had made with Yahuḏah and Yahonathan his brothers;
14.19: writings which were read before the assembly at Yerushalayim.
14.20: And this is the copy of the letters that the Lakedaemonians sent: “The rulers of the Lakedaemonians, with the city, to Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol, and the elders, and kohenim, and remnant of the people of the Yahuḏim, our brothers, greetings.
14.21: “The ambassadors that were sent to our people informed us of your esteem and honor, therefore we were glad of their coming,
14.22: and registered the words that they spoke in the council of the people in this manner: ‘Numĕnios son of Antioḵos, and Antipater son of Yason, the Yahuḏim’s ambassadors, came to us to renew the friendship they had with us,
14.23: and it pleased the people to receive the men honorably, and to put the copy of their message in public record, so that the people of the Lakedaemonians might have a memorial of it. Furthermore we have written a copy of it to Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol.’ ”
14.24: After this Shim’on sent Numĕnios to Rome with a great golden shield of one thousand minas weight to confirm the alliance with them.
14.25: When the people heard of this, they said, “What thanks shall we give to Shim’on and his sons?
14.26: “For he and his brothers and the house of his father have established Yisra’ĕl, and chased away their enemies from them in battle, and confirmed their freedom.”
14.27: So then they wrote it on tablets of bronze, which they placed on columns in Mount Tsiyon. And this is the copy of the writing: “The eighteenth day of the month Elul, in the hundred and seventy-second year, being the third year of Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol,
14.28: at Asaramel in the great assembly of the kohenim and people and rulers of the nation and elders of the country, these words were declared to us.
14.29: “Since many times there have been battles in the country, for which the maintenance of their Miqdash, and the Torah, Shim’on the son of Mattithyahu, of the descendants of Yariḇ, together with his brothers, put themselves in danger, and resisting the enemies of their nation did their nation great honor.
14.30: “For after Yahonathan, having gathered his nation together, and been their kohĕn ha’gadol, was added to his people,
14.31: their enemies prepared to invade their country, that they might destroy it, and lay hands on the Miqdash.
14.32: “At which time Shim’on rose up, and fought for his nation, and spent much of his own wealth, and armed the brave men of his nation and gave them wages,
14.33: and fortified the cities of Yahuḏah, together with Bĕyth Tsur that lies on the borders of Yahuḏah, where the armor of the enemies had been before; but he positioned a garrison of Yahuḏim there.
14.34: “He also fortified Yapho, which lies on the coast, and Gezer, that borders on Ashdoḏ, where the enemies had dwelt before. And he appointed Yahuḏim there, and supplied them with all matters necessary for its repairs.”
14.35: So the people sang the deeds of Shim’on, and to what esteem he thought to bring his nation, making him their governor and chief kohĕn, because he had done all these matters, and for the Right-Ruling and belief which he guarded for his nation, and that by all means he sought to exalt his people.
14.36: For in his time matters prospered in his hands, so that the gentiles were taken out of their country, and also those that were in the city of Dawiḏ in Yerushalayim who had made themselves a tower from which they came out and polluted all around the Miqdash and did much evil in the qodesh place.
14.37: But he appointed Yahuḏim in it and fortified it for the safety of the country and the city, and raised up the walls of Yerushalayim.
14.38: Meleḵ Dĕmĕtrios also confirmed him in the high kehunnah according to those matters,
14.39: and made him one of his friends, and honored him with great honor.
14.40: For he had heard it said, that the Romans had called the Yahuḏim their friends and allies and brothers; and that they had entertained the ambassadors of Shim’on honorably.
14.41: Also that the Yahuḏim and kohenim were well pleased that Shim’on should be their governor and kohĕn ha’gadol forever, until there should arise a trustworthy naḇi.
14.42: That he should also be their leader, and would take charge of the Miqdash, to appoint them over their works, and over the country, and over the armory, and over the fortresses.
14.43: Besides this, that he should be obeyed by every man, and that all the writings in the country should be made in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple and wear gold.
14.44: Also that it should be not allowed for the people or kohenim to break any of these matters, or to refute his words, or to gather an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or wear a gold buckle;
14.45: and whoever should do otherwise, or break any of these matters should be punished.
14.46: So it pleased all the people to establish Shim’on, and to do as had been said.
14.47: Then Shim’on accepted this, and was well pleased to be kohĕn ha’gadol, and leader and governor of the Yahuḏim and kohenim, and to defend them all.
14.48: So they commanded that this writing should be put on tablets of bronze, and that they should be put up within the surrounds of the Miqdash in a conspicuous place;
14.49: also that the copies of this should be stored in the treasury, so that Shim’on and his sons might have them.

15.1: Now Antioḵos son of Dĕmĕtrios the meleḵ sent letters from the islands of the sea to Shim’on the kohĕn and prince of the Yahuḏim, and to all the people;
15.2: the contents of which were these: “Meleḵ Antioḵos to Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol and leader of his nation, and to the people of the Yahuḏim, greetings.
15.3: “Since some troublesome men have usurped the reign of our fathers, and my purpose is to challenge it again that I may restore it to the old estate, and to that end have gathered a multitude of foreign soldiers together and prepared ships of battle;
15.4: my purpose also being to go through the country that I may be avenged of those that have destroyed it and made many cities in the reign desolate.
15.5: “Now therefore I confirm to you all the offerings which the melaḵim before me granted you, and also whatever gifts they granted.
15.6: “I allow you to coin silver for your country with your own stamp.
15.7: “And concerning Yerushalayim and the Miqdash; let them be free, and all the armor that you have made, and fortresses that you have built, and keep in your hands, let them remain with you.
15.8: “And if whatever is, or shall be, owing to the meleḵ, let it be forgiven you from this time on forever.
15.9: “Furthermore, when we have obtained our reign, we will honor you, and your nation, and your Hĕyḵal, with great honor, so that your honor shall be known throughout the world.”
15.10: In the hundred and seventy-fourth year Antioḵos went into the land of his fathers, at which time all the forces came together to him, so that few were left with Truphon.
15.11: Therefore being pursued by Meleḵ Antioḵos, he fled to Dora, which lies by the sea coast,
15.12: for he saw that troubles came upon him all at once, and that his forces had deserted him.
15.13: Then Antioḵos encamped against Dora, having with him a hundred and twenty thousand men of battle, and eight thousand horsemen.
15.14: And when he had surrounded the city and linked ships close to the town on the sea coast, he troubled the city by land and by sea, neither did he allow any to go out or in.
15.15: In the winter Numĕnios and his army came from Rome, having letters to the melaḵim and countries in which were written these matters:
15.16: “Lukios, consul of the Romans to Meleḵ Ptolemaeus, greetings.
15.17: “The Yahuḏim’s ambassadors, our friends and allies, came to us to renew the old friendship and alliance, being sent from Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol and from the people of the Yahuḏim,
15.18: and they brought a gold shield of one thousand minas.
15.19: “We thought it good therefore to write to the melaḵim and countries, that they should do them no harm, nor fight against them, their cities, or countries, nor indeed aid their enemies against them.
15.20: “It also seemed good to us to receive the shield from them.
15.21: “If therefore there are any troublesome fellows, that have fled from their country to you, deliver them to Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol, that he may punish them according to their own Torah.”
15.22: He also wrote the same words to Dĕmĕtrios the meleḵ, and Attalus, to Ariarathĕs, and Arsakĕs,
15.23: and to all the countries and to Lampsakos, and the Lakedaemonians and to Dĕlos and Mundos and Sikion and Karia and Samos and Pamphulia and Lukia and Halikarnassos and Rhodos and Arados and Kos and Sidĕ and Aradus and Gortina and Knidos and Kupros and Kurĕnĕ.
15.24: And the copy of this they wrote to Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol.
15.25: So Antioḵos the meleḵ encamped against Dora the second day, assaulting it continually, and making siege engines by which means he shut up Truphon, that he could neither go out nor go in.
15.26: At that time Shim’on sent him two thousand chosen men to aid him; also silver and gold and much armor.
15.27: Nevertheless he would not receive them, but broke all the covenants which he had made with him before, and became hostile toward him.
15.28: Furthermore he sent Athĕnobius, one of his friends to him, to speak with him, and say, “You withhold Yapho and Gezer - with the tower that is in Yerushalayim - which are cities of my reign.
15.29: “You have destroyed its borders, and done great evil in the land, and taken the rule of many places within my reign.
15.30: “Now therefore, deliver the cities which you have taken, and the tributes of the places, of which you have taken rule outside the borders of Yahuḏah;
15.31: or else give me five hundred talanton of silver for them and for the damage that you have done, and the tributes of the cities - another five hundred talanton. If not, we will come and fight against you.”
15.32: So Athĕnobius the meleḵ’s friend came to Yerushalayim, and when he saw the esteem of Shim’on, and the storage of gold and silver plate and his great attendance, he was astonished and told him the meleḵ’s message.
15.33: Then Shim’on answered and said to him, “We have neither taken other men’s land, nor held that which belongs to others, but the inheritance of our fathers which our enemies held wrongfully in possession for a certain time.
15.34: “Therefore we, having opportunity, hold the inheritance of our fathers.
15.35: “And whereas you demand Yapho and Gezer - although they did great harm to the people in our country - yet we will give you a hundred talanton for them.” To this Athĕnobius answered him not a word,
15.36: but returned in a rage to the meleḵ, and reported these words to him, and of the esteem of Shim’on, and of all that he had seen. So the meleḵ was exceedingly wroth.
15.37: In the meantime, Truphon fled by ship to Orthosia.
15.38: Then the meleḵ made Kendĕbeus captain of the sea coast, and gave him an army of footmen and horsemen,
15.39: and commanded him to move his army toward Yahuḏah. He also commanded him to build up Qiḏron, and to fortify the gates, and to fight against the people. But as for the meleḵ himself, he pursued Truphon.
15.40: So Kendĕbeus came to Yaḇneh and began to provoke the people and to invade Yahuḏah, and to take the people captive and slay them.
15.41: And when he had built up Qiḏron, he positioned horsemen there, and an army of footmen, so that coming out they might make attacks on the roads to Yahuḏah, as the meleḵ had commanded him.

16.1: Then Yoḥanan came up from Gezer, and told Shim’on his father what Kendĕbeus had done.
16.2: Therefore Shim’on called his two eldest sons Yahuḏah and Yoḥanan and said to them, “My brothers and I and my father’s house have from my youth to this day always fought against the enemies of Yisra’ĕl. And matters have prospered so well in our hands, that we have delivered Yisra’ĕl many times.
16.3: “But now I am old, and you, by Elohim’s kindness, are of a sufficient age. You take the place of myself and my brother, and go and fight for our nation, and the help the shamayim be with you.”
16.4: So he chose twenty thousand men of battle out of the country with horsemen, who went out against Kendĕbeus, and rested that night at Modi’im.
16.5: And when as they rose in the morning, and went into the plain, see, a mighty great army of both footmen and horsemen came against them. However, there was a wadi of water between them,
16.6: so he and his people encamped opposite them. But when he saw that the people were afraid to go over the wadi of water, he went over first himself, and then the men seeing him, passed over after him.
16.7: That done, he divided his men, and positioned the horsemen in the midst of the footmen, for the enemy’s horsemen were very numerous.
16.8: Then they sounded with the qodesh trumpets, so Kendĕbeus and his army were put to flight, so that many of them were slain, and the remnant went to the stronghold.
16.9: At that time Yahuḏah, Yoḥanan’s brother was wounded; but Yoḥanan still pursued them until he came to Qiḏron which Kendĕbeus had built.
16.10: So they fled even to the towers in the fields of Ashdoḏ; therefore he burned it with fire, so that there were about two thousand of them slain. Afterward he returned to the land of Yahuḏah in peace.
16.11: And in the plain of Yeriḥo Ptolemaeus the son of Aboubus was made captain, and he had an abundance of silver and gold,
16.12: for he was the kohĕn ha’gadol’s son-in-law.
16.13: Therefore his heart being lifted up, he thought to take the land for himself, and therefore planned deceitfully against Shim’on and his sons to destroy them.
16.14: Now Shim’on was visiting the cities that were in the country and taking care for the good ordering of them; at which time he himself came down to Yeriḥo with his sons Mattithyahu and Yahuḏah, in the hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month called Sheḇat,
16.15: where the son of Aboubus, receiving them deceitfully into a small fortress called Doḵ - which he had built - made them a great feast. However, he had men hidden there.
16.16: So when Shim’on and his sons had drunk plenty, Ptolemaeus and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Shim’on into the feasting place, and slew him, and his two sons, and some of his servants.
16.17: In doing so, he committed a great treachery, and repaid evil for good.
16.18: Then Ptolemaeus wrote these matters, and sent to the meleḵ, that he should send him an army to aid him, and he would deliver him the land and cities.
16.19: He also sent others to Gezer to kill Yoḥanan. And he sent letters to the tribunes to come to him, that he might give them silver and gold and rewards.
16.20: And others he sent to take Yerushalayim and the mountain of the Hĕyḵal.
16.21: Now one had run before to Gezer and told Yoḥanan that his father and brothers were slain, and he said, “Ptolemaeus has sent to slay you also.”
16.22: When he heard of this, he was greatly astonished, so he took hold of those that came to destroy him, and slew them; for he knew that they sought to take him away.
16.23: Concerning the rest of the acts of Yoḥanan, and his battles, and worthy deeds which he did, and the building of the walls which he made, and his doings,
16.24: see, these are written in the chronicles of his kehunnah, from the time he was made kohĕn ha’gadol after his father.

2.1: In those days Mattithyahu the son of Yoḥanan, the son of Shim’on, a kohĕn of the sons of Yoyariḇ, came from Yerushalayim, and dwelt in Modi’im.
2.2: And he had five sons: Yoḥanan, called Gaddi;
2.5: Eli’ezer, called Aḇaran; and Yahonathan, who was also called Apphus.
2.6: And when he saw the blasphemies that were committed in Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim,
2.7: he said, “Woe is me! Why was I born to see this misery of my people, and of the qodesh city, and to dwell there, when it was delivered into the hand of the enemy, and the Miqdash into the hand of foreigners?
2.8: “Her Hĕyḵal has become as a man without esteem.
2.9: “Her splendid utensils are carried away into captivity, her infants are slain in the streets, her young men - with the sword of the enemy.
2.10: “What nation has not had a part in her reign and received of her spoils?
2.11: “All her adornments are taken away; from a free woman she has become a slave!
2.12: “And, see, our Miqdash, even our splendor and our esteem, is laid waste, and the gentiles have profaned it.
2.13: “Why therefore shall we live any longer?”
2.14: Then Mattithyahu and his sons tore their garments, and put on sackcloth, and mourned greatly.
2.15: In the meantime, the meleḵ’s officers, who compelled the people to revolt, came into the city of Modi’im, to make them offer.
2.16: And when many of Yisra’ĕl came to them, Mattithyahu and his sons also came together.
2.17: Then the meleḵ’s officers answered and spoke to Mattithyahu in this way: “You are a ruler, and an honorable and great man in this city, and strengthened with sons and brothers.
2.18: “Now therefore, you come first and complete the meleḵ’s command, as all the gentiles have done, and also the men of Yahuḏah, and those who remain at Yerushalayim, so you and your house shall be in the number of the meleḵ’s friends, and you and your children shall be honored with silver and gold, and many rewards.”
2.19: Then Mattithyahu answered and spoke with a loud voice, “Though all the nations that are under the meleḵ’s reign obey him, and every one falls away from the belief of their fathers, and gives consent to his commands,
2.20: still my sons and my brothers and I will walk in the Covenant of our fathers.
2.21: “Elohim forbid that we should forsake the Torah and the Laws!
2.22: “We will not listen to the meleḵ’s words, to go from our belief, either to the right hand, or the left.”
2.23: Now when he had finished speaking these words, one of the Yahuḏim came in the sight of all to offer on the altar which was at Modi’im, according to the meleḵ’s command.
2.24: When Mattithyahu saw this matter, he burned with ardor, and he trembled within, neither could he refrain to show his wrath according to righteousness. Therefore he ran, and slew him upon the altar.
2.25: At that time, he also killed the meleḵ’s commissioner, who compelled men to offer, and he pulled down the altar.
2.26: Thus he dealt with ardor for the Torah of Elohim as Pineḥas did toward Zimri the son of Sallu.
2.27: And Mattithyahu cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, “Whoever is ardent for the Torah, and continues in the Covenant, let him follow me!”
2.28: So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that they had in the city.
2.29: Then many that sought after right-ruling and judgment went down into the wilderness, to dwell there,
2.30: both they and their children, and their wives, and their cattle, because afflictions increased greatly upon them.
2.31: Now when it was told to the meleḵ’s servants, and the army that was at Yerushalayim, in the city of Dawiḏ, that some men who had broken the meleḵ’s command had gone down into the hiding places in the wilderness,
2.32: they pursued after them in great number, and having overtaken them, they encamped against them, and fought against them on the Shabbath day.
2.33: And they said to them, “Let that which you have done until now be enough! Come out, and do according to the command of the meleḵ, and you shall live.”
2.34: But they said, “We do not come out, neither shall we do the meleḵ’s command, to profane the Shabbath day!”
2.35: So then they fought them in haste.
2.36: However they did not answer them, neither threw a stone at them, nor disclosed the places where they lay hid,
2.37: but said, “Let us die all in our innocence. The shamayim and earth will witness for us, that you put us to death wrongfully.”
2.38: So they rose up against them in battle on the Shabbath, and they slew them, with their wives and children and their cattle, to the number of one thousand people.
2.39: Now when Mattithyahu and his friends heard of this, they mourned for them greatly.
2.40: And one of them said to another, “If we all do as our brothers have done, and do not fight for our lives and Laws against the gentiles, they will now quickly destroy us from the earth.”
2.41: At that time therefore they agreed, saying, “Whoever shall come to fight with us on the Shabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we all die as our brothers that were murdered in the hiding places.”
2.42: Then an army of Ḥasiḏim came to him, who were mighty men of Yisra’ĕl, even all those who were voluntarily dedicated to the Torah.
2.43: Also all those that fled from persecution joined themselves them, and were a support to them.
2.44: So they joined their forces, and smote sinful men in their wrath, and wicked men in their wrath; but the rest fled to the gentiles for support.
2.45: Then Mattithyahu and his friends went round about, and pulled down the altars.
2.46: And whatever uncircumcised children they found within the borders of Yisra’ĕl, those they courageously circumcised.
2.47: They also pursued after the proud men, and the work prospered in their hand.
2.48: So they retained the Torah from the hand of the gentiles, and out of the hand of melaḵim, neither did they allow the sinner to overcome.
2.49: Now when the time drew near that Mattithyahu would die, he said to his sons, “Excellence and rebuke has now gained strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of displeasure.
2.50: “Now therefore my sons, be ardent for the Torah, and give your lives for the Covenant of your fathers.
2.51: “Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time; so shall you receive great honor and an everlasting name.
2.52: “Was not Aḇraham found trustworthy in temptation, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness?
2.53: “Yosĕph in the time of his distress kept the Command and was made master of Mitsrayim.
2.54: “Pineḥas our father in being ardent and fervent obtained the Covenant of an everlasting kehunnah.
2.55: “Yahoshua for filling the Word was made a judge in Yisra’ĕl.
2.56: “Kalĕḇ for bearing witness before the assembly received the inheritance of the land.
2.57: “Dawiḏ for being kind possessed the throne of an everlasting reign.
2.58: “Ĕliyahu for being ardent and fervent for the Torah was taken up into the shamayim.
2.59: “Ḥananyah, Azaryah, and Misha’ĕl were saved out of the fire by belief.
2.60: “Dani’ĕl for his innocence was delivered from the mouth of lions.
2.61: “And so consider throughout all the ages, that none that put their trust in Him shall be overcome.
2.62: “Do not fear then the words of a sinful man; for his esteem shall be dung and worms.
2.63: “Today he may be lifted up, but tomorrow he shall not be found, because he has returned to his dust, and his plans have come to naught.
2.64: “Therefore, you my sons, be brave and show yourselves men on behalf of the Torah; for by It you shall obtain esteem.
2.65: “And see, I know that your brother Shim’on is a man of counsel, listen to him always. He shall be a father to you.
2.66: “As for Yahuḏah Maqqaḇah, he has been mighty and strong, even from his youth. Let him be your captain, and fight the battle of the people.
2.67: “Also receive all those that observe the Torah, and avenge the wrong of your people.
2.68: “Repay the gentiles completely, and guard the Commands of the Torah.”
2.69: So he baraḵ them, and was gathered to his fathers.
2.70: And he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year, and his sons buried him in the tomb of his fathers at Modi’im, and all Yisra’ĕl made a great lamentation for him.

3.1: Then his son Yahuḏah, called Maqqaḇah, rose up in his place.
3.2: And all his brothers aided him, and so did all they that stood with his father, and they fought the battle for Yisra’ĕl with eagerness.
3.3: So he gave his people great honor, and put on a breastplate as a giant, and girded his armor about him, and he fought, protecting the army with his sword.
3.4: In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion’s cub roaring for his prey.
3.5: For He pursued the wicked, and sought them out, and burned up those that oppressed his people.
3.6: Therefore the wicked shrunk for fear of him, and all the workers of wickedness were troubled, because deliverance prospered in his hand.
3.7: He also grieved many melaḵim, and made Ya’aqoḇ glad with his deeds, and his remembrance is a beraḵah forever.
3.8: And he went through the cities of Yahuḏah, destroying the wicked out of them, and turning away wrath from Yisra’ĕl,
3.9: so that he was renowned to the utmost ends of the earth, and he received to himself those who were ready to perish.
3.10: Then Apollonios gathered the gentiles together, and a great army out of Shomeron to fight against Yisra’ĕl.
3.11: When Yahuḏah knew of this, he went out to meet him, and so he smote him, and slew him. Many also fell down slain, but the rest fled.
3.12: Therefore Yahuḏah took their spoils, and also the sword of Apollonios, and he fought with it all his lifetime.
3.13: Now when Seron, a prince of the army of Suria, heard that Yahuḏah had gathered a multitude to himself and an army of the trustworthy to go out with him to battle;
3.14: he said, “I will make myself a name and reign in honor; for I will go fight with Yahuḏah and those that are with him, who despise the meleḵ’s command.”
3.15: So he prepared to go up, and a mighty army of the wicked went with him to help him, and to be avenged on the children of Yisra’ĕl.
3.16: And when he came near to the ascent of Bĕyth Ḥoron, Yahuḏah went out to meet him with a small army,
3.17: who, when they saw the army coming to meet them, said to Yahuḏah, “How shall we be able, being so few, to fight against so great a multitude and so strong, seeing we are ready to faint from fasting all this day?”
3.18: Yahuḏah answered them, “It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the Elohim of the shamayim it is all the same - to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company,
3.19: for the overcoming of battle stands not in the multitude of an army; but strength comes from the shamayim.
3.20: “They come against us in great pride and wickedness to destroy us with our wives and children, and to plunder us,
3.21: but we fight for our lives and our Laws.
3.22: “Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself will overthrow them before our face. And as for you, do not be afraid of them.”
3.23: Now as soon as he had ended speaking, he rushed upon them suddenly, and so Seron and his army was overthrown before him.
3.24: And they pursued them from the descent of Bĕyth Ḥoron to the plain, where about eight hundred men of them were slain; and the remainder fled into the land of the Pelishtites.
3.25: Then the fear of Yahuḏah and his brothers began, and an exceedingly great dread, fell upon the nations round about them,
3.26: so that the report of him came to the meleḵ, and all nations spoke of the battles of Yahuḏah.
3.27: Now when meleḵ Antioḵos heard these matters, he was full of wrath, therefore he sent and gathered together all the armies of his reign, even a very strong army.
3.28: He also opened his treasury, and gave his soldiers wages for a year, commanding them to be ready whenever he needed them.
3.29: Nevertheless, when he saw that the silver of his treasures was spent and that the taxes in the country were small, because of the uprising and plague, which he had brought upon the land in taking away the Laws which had been of old;
3.30: he feared that he would not be able to bear the expenses any longer, nor to have such gifts to give so liberally as he did before, for he had exceeded the melaḵim that were before him.
3.31: Therefore, being greatly perplexed in his mind, he determined to go to Paras, to take the taxes from the lands, and to gather much silver.
3.32: So he left Lusias, a nobleman, and one of royal blood, to oversee the affairs of the meleḵ from the River Perath to the borders of Mitsrayim,
3.33: and to raise his son Antioḵos, until he came again.
3.34: And he delivered to him half of his armies and the elephants, and gave him charge of all matters that he would have done, and also concerning those that dwelt in Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim,
3.35: that is, that he should send an army against them to destroy and uproot the strength of Yisra’ĕl, and the remnant of Yerushalayim, and to remove their remembrance from that place,
3.36: and that he should place foreigners in all their places, and divide their land by lot.
3.37: So the meleḵ took the half of the armies that remained, and departed from Antioḵeia, his royal city in the hundred and forty-seventh year; and having passed over the River Perath, he went through the high countries.
3.38: Then Lusias chose Ptolemaeus the son of Dorumĕnĕs, Nikanor, and Gorgias, mighty men of the meleḵ’s friends,
3.39: and he sent forty thousand footmen with them, and seven thousand horsemen, to go into the land of Yahuḏah, and destroy it, as the meleḵ commanded.
3.40: So they went out with all their strength, and came and encamped by Amma’us in the plains country.
3.41: And the merchants of the country, hearing the report of them, took very much silver and gold, with servants, and came to the camp to buy the children of Yisra’ĕl as slaves. A strength from Suria and of the land of the Pelishtites also joined themselves to them.
3.42: Now when Yahuḏah and his brothers saw that hardships were multiplied, and that the armies encamped themselves on their borders, for they knew how the meleḵ had given command to destroy the people, and utterly annihilate them,
3.43: they said one to another, “Let us restore the fallen state of our people, and let us fight for our people and the Miqdash.”
3.44: Then there was an assembly gathered together, that they might be ready for battle, and that they might pray, and ask for favor and compassion.
3.45: Now Yerushalayim lay as empty as a wilderness; there was none of her children that went in or out. The Miqdash was also trodden down, and foreigners guarded the stronghold; the gentiles had their dwelling in that place and joy was taken from Ya’aqoḇ, and the flute with the harp had ceased.
