3.46: Therefore the Yisra’ĕlites assembled themselves together, and came to Mitspah, opposite Yerushalayim; for in Mitspah was the place where they previously prayed in Yisra’ĕl.
3.47: Then they fasted that day, and put on sackcloth, and threw ashes on their heads, and tore their garments,
3.48: and laid open the Book of the Torah, wherein the gentiles had sought to paint the likeness of their images.
3.49: They also brought the garments of the kohenim, and the first-fruits, and the tithes, and they brought up the Nazirites, who had completed their days.
3.50: Then they cried with a loud voice toward the shamayim saying, “What shall we do with these, and to where shall we carry them away?
3.51: “For Your Miqdash is trodden down and profaned, and Your kohenim are in despair, and brought low.
3.52: “And see, the gentiles have assembled together against us to destroy us! What they devise against us, You know.
3.53: “How shall we be able to stand against them, unless You, O Elohim, are our Help?”
3.54: Then they sounded with trumpets, and cried with a loud voice.
3.55: And after this Yahuḏah appointed commanders over the people, even commanders over thousands, and over hundreds, and over fifties, and over tens.
3.56: But as for those that were building houses, or were engaged to wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, those he commanded that they should return, every man to his own house, according to the Torah.
3.57: So the camp moved, and encamped on the south side of Amma’us.
3.58: And Yahuḏah said, “Arm yourselves, and be brave men, and see that you are ready before the morning to fight with these nations that are assembled together against us to destroy us and our Miqdash.
3.59: “For it is better for us to die in battle, than to see the destruction of our people and our Miqdash.
3.60: “Nevertheless, according to the desire of Elohim in the shamayim, so let Him do.

4.1: Then Gorgias took five thousand footmen, and one thousand of the best horsemen, and moved out of the camp by night,
4.2: so that he might charge in upon the camp of the Yahuḏim, and smite them suddenly; and the men of the fortress were his guides.
4.3: Now when Yahuḏah heard of this, he relocated himself, and the brave men with him, that he might smite the meleḵ’s army which was at Amma’us,
4.4: while as yet, the armies were dispersed from the camp.
4.5: In the meantime Gorgias came into the camp of Yahuḏah by night, and when he found no one there, he sought them in the mountains, for he said, “These men flee from us!”
4.6: But as soon as it was day, Yahuḏah showed himself in the plain with three thousand men, who however had neither armor nor swords at hand.
4.7: And they saw the camp of the gentiles, that it was strong and well armed, and surrounded with horsemen; and these were arranged for battle.
4.8: Then Yahuḏah said to the men that were with him, “Do not fear their multitude, neither be afraid of their attack.
4.9: “Remember how our fathers were delivered in the Sea of Reeds, when Pharaoh pursued them with an army.
4.10: “Now therefore, let us cry unto the shamayim. It might be that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shows favor upon us, and remembers the Covenant of our fathers, and destroy this army before our face this day,
4.11: so that all the gentiles may know that there is One who delivers and saves Yisra’ĕl.”
4.12: Then the foreigners lifted up their eyes, and saw them coming over against them,
4.13: therefore they went out of the camp to battle; and those that were with Yahuḏah sounded their trumpets.
4.14: So they joined in battle, and the gentiles, being defeated, fled into the plain.
4.15: However all those in the rear were slain with the sword, for they pursued them to Gezer, and to the plains of Eḏom, and Ashdoḏ, and Yaḇneh, so that around three thousand men of them were slain.
4.16: This done, Yahuḏah returned again with his army from pursuing them,
4.17: and said to the people, “Do not be greedy for the spoil, because there is a battle before us,
4.18: and Gorgias and his army are here by us in the mountain. But stand now against our enemies, and overcome them, and after this you may boldly take the spoils.”
4.19: As Yahuḏah was still speaking these words, there appeared a group of them looking out from the mountain;
4.20: who saw that the Yahuḏim had put their army to flight and were burning the tents, for the smoke that was seen revealed what was done.
4.21: Therefore when they saw these matters, they were very afraid, and also seeing the army of Yahuḏah in the plain ready to fight,
4.22: they fled, every one into the land of foreigners.
4.23: Then Yahuḏah returned to plunder the tents, where they took much gold, and silver, and blue silk, and purple of the sea, and great riches.
4.24: After this they went home, and sung a song of thanksgiving, and baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the shamayim, because He is good, because His kindness endures forever.
4.25: Therefore Yisra’ĕl had a great deliverance that day.
4.26: Now all the foreigners that had escaped came and told Lusias what had come to be,
4.27: who, when he heard of it, was ashamed and discouraged, because matters that he would not have done were done to Yisra’ĕl, nor such matters as the meleḵ commanded him had come to pass.
4.28: Therefore the next year following, Lusias gathered together sixty thousand chosen footmen, and five thousand horsemen, that he might subdue them.
4.29: So they came to Eḏom, and pitched their tents at Bĕyth Tsur; and Yahuḏah met them with ten thousand men.
4.30: And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, “Baruḵ are you, O Savior of Yisra’ĕl, who calmed the violence of the mighty by the hand of your servant Dawiḏ, and gave the army of foreigners into the hands of Yahonathan the son of Sha’ul, and his armor bearer.
4.31: “Deliver this army into the hand of your people Yisra’ĕl, and let them be put to shame in their strength and horsemen.
4.32: “Cause them to be weakened, and make the boldness of their strength fall away, and let them quake at their destruction.
4.33: “Throw them down with the sword of those that love You, and let all those that know Your Name praise You with thanksgiving!”
4.34: So they joined in battle, and there were about five thousand men of the army of Lusias slain; so they were slain before them.
4.35: Now when Lusias saw his army put to flight, and the bravery of Yahuḏah’s soldiers, and how they were ready either to live or die bravely, he went to Antioḵeia, and gathered together an army of foreigners. And having made his army greater than it was, he prepared to come again to Yahuḏah.
4.36: Then Yahuḏah and his brothers said, “See, our enemies are defeated, let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the Miqdash.”
4.37: After this, all the army assembled themselves together and went up to Mount Tsiyon.
4.38: And when they saw the Miqdash desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest, or in one of the mountains, and also the rooms of the kohenim pulled down,
4.39: they tore their garments, and made a great lamentation, and threw ashes on their heads,
4.40: and fell down flat to the ground on their faces, and blew an alarm with the trumpets, and cried toward the shamayim.
4.41: Then Yahuḏah appointed some men to fight against those that were in the fortress, until he had cleansed the Miqdash.
4.42: So he chose kohenim of qodesh behavior, who took delight in the Torah;
4.43: who cleansed the Miqdash, and carried out the defiled stones to an unclean place.
4.44: And when they consulted what to do with the altar of burnt offerings, which was profaned;
4.45: they thought it best to pull it down, lest it should be a reproach to them, because the gentiles had defiled it. Therefore they pulled it down,
4.46: and laid up the stones in the mountain of the Hĕyḵal in a suitable place, until there should come a naḇi to show what should be done with them.
4.47: Then they took whole stones according to the Torah, and built a new altar according to the former,
4.48: and built up the Miqdash, and that which was within the Hĕyḵal, and qadosh the courts.
4.49: They also made new qodesh vessels, and they brought the lampstand into the Hĕyḵal, and the altar of burnt offerings, and of incense, and the table.
4.50: And they burned incense upon the altar, and they lit the lamps that were on the lampstand, that they might give light in the Hĕyḵal.
4.51: Furthermore they put the loaves on the table, and spread out the veils, and finished all the works which they had begun to do.
4.52: Now on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Kislĕw, in the hundred and forty-eighth year, they rose up early in the morning,
4.53: and offered an offering according to the Torah upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made.
4.54: Even, at the time and the day the gentiles had profaned it, even in that it was dedicated with songs, and stringed instruments, and harps, and cymbals.
4.55: Then all the people fell on their faces, as they worshipped and baraḵ the Elohim of the shamayim, who had given them good success.
4.56: And so they guarded the dedication of the altar eight days and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and slaughtered the offering of deliverance and praise.
4.57: They also adorned the front of the Hĕyḵal with crowns of gold, and with shields; and they renewed the gates and the rooms, and hung doors upon them.
4.58: Therefore there was very great joy among the people, because the reproach of the gentiles was removed.
4.59: And Yahuḏah and his brothers with the whole assembly of Yisra’ĕl ordained that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year over eight days, from the twenty-fifth day of the month Kislĕw, with joy and gladness.
4.60: At that time they also built up Mount Tsiyon with high walls and strong towers round about, lest the gentiles should come and trample it down as they had done before.
4.61: And they appointed a garrison there to guard it, and fortified Bĕyth Tsur to guard it; that the people might have a defense against Eḏom.

5.1: Now when the nations round about heard that the altar was built and the Miqdash renewed as before, it displeased them very much.
5.2: Therefore they thought to destroy the generation of Ya’aqoḇ that was among them, and so they began to slay and destroy the people.
5.3: Then Yahuḏah fought against the children of Ĕsaw in Eḏom at Aqrabbim, because they besieged Ga’al. And he gave them a great overthrow, and weakened their resolve, and took their spoil.
5.4: He also remembered the wrong of the children of Be’an, who had been a snare and an offense to the people, in that they lay in wait for them in the ways.
5.5: Therefore He enclosed them in the towers, and encamped against them, and destroyed them utterly, and burned the towers of that place with fire, and all that were in them.
5.6: Afterward, he passed over to the children of Ammon, where he found many people of great strength, with Timotheos their captain.
5.7: So he fought many battles with them, till at length they were defeated before him; and he smote them.
5.8: And when he had taken Ya’zĕr, with the towns belonging to it, he returned to Yahuḏah.
5.9: Then the gentiles that were at Gil’aḏ assembled themselves together against the Yisra’ĕlites that were in their borders, to destroy them. But they fled to the fortress of Dathema,
5.10: and sent letters to Yahuḏah and his brothers: “The gentiles that are round about us are assembled together against us to destroy us,
5.11: and they are preparing to come and take the fortress where we have fled, Timotheos being captain of their army.
5.12: “Come now therefore, and deliver us from their hands, for many of us are slain.
5.13: “Even all our brothers that were in the places of Toḇ are put to death. They have also taken their wives and their children captive, and carried away their goods, and they have destroyed about one thousand men there.”
5.14: While these letters were still being read, see, other messengers came from Galil with their garments torn, who reported on this way,
5.15: and said, “They of Ptolemais, and of Tsor, and Tsiḏon, and all Galil of the gentiles, are assembled together against us to destroy us!”
5.16: Now when Yahuḏah and the people heard these words, there assembled a great assembly together, to consult what they should do for their brothers who were in trouble, and under attack.
5.17: Then Yahuḏah said to Shim’on his brother, “Choose men, and go and deliver your brothers that are in Galil, for I and Yahonathan my brother will go into the country of Gil’aḏ.”
5.18: So he left Yosĕph the son of Zeḵaryah, and Azaryah, captains of the people, with the remainder of the army in Yahuḏah to guard it;
5.19: to whom he gave command, saying, “Take charge of this people, and see that you do not fight against the gentiles until the time that we return.”
5.20: Now to Shim’on were given three thousand men to go to Galil, and to Yahuḏah, eight thousand men for the country of Gil’aḏ.
5.21: Then Shim’on went to Galil, where he fought many battles with the gentiles, so that the gentiles were defeated by him.
5.22: And he pursued them to the gate of Ptolemais, and about three thousand men of the gentiles were slain, whose spoil he took.
5.23: And those that were in Galil and in Araḇoth with their wives and their children and all that they had, he took away with him, and brought them to Yahuḏah with great joy.
5.24: Yahuḏah Maqqaḇah and his brother Yahonathan also went over the Yardĕn, and traveled three days’ journey in the wilderness,
5.25: where they met with the Naḇothites who came to them in a peaceable manner, and told them all that had befallen their brothers in the land of Gil’aḏ,
5.26: and how many of them were shut up in Botsrah, and Besor, and Almon, Kaphtor, Maqqĕḏah, and Qarnayim - all these cities, strong and great -
5.27: and that they were shut up in the rest of the cities of the country of Gil’aḏ, and that the next day they had appointed to bring their army against the forts, and to take them, and to destroy them all in one day.
5.28: So Yahuḏah and his army turned suddenly by the way of the wilderness to Botsrah; and when he had won the city, he slew all the males with the edge of the sword and took all their spoil, and burned the city with fire.
5.29: From there he moved by night, and went till he came to the fortress.
5.30: And early in the morning they looked up, and see, there was an innumerable multitude carrying ladders and other engines of battle, to take the fortress, for they assaulted them.
5.31: Therefore when Yahuḏah saw that the battle had begun, and that the cry of the city went up to the shamayim, with trumpets, and a great noise,
5.32: he said to his army, “Fight this day for your brothers!”
5.33: So he went out behind them in three companies, who sounded their trumpets, and cried with prayer.
5.34: Then the army of Timotheos, knowing that it was Maqqaḇah, fled from him. Therefore he smote them with a great slaughter, so that about eight thousand men of them were killed that day.
5.35: This done, Yahuḏah turned aside to Mitspah; and after he had attacked it, he took and slew all the males there, and took the spoil from there and burned it with fire.
5.36: From there, he went and took Kasphor, Meḡiddo, Besor, and the other cities of the country of Gil’aḏ.
5.37: After these events, Timotheos gathered another army and encamped against Raphah beyond the wadi.
5.38: So Yahuḏah sent men to spy out the army, who brought him word saying, “All the gentiles that are round about us are assembled to them, even a very great army.
5.39: “He has also hired the Araḇians to help them and they have pitched their tents beyond the wadi, ready to come and fight against you.” Hearing this Yahuḏah went to meet them.
5.40: Then Timotheos said to the captains of his army, “When Yahuḏah and his army come near the wadi, if he passes over to us first, we shall not be able to withstand him; for he will mightily overcome us.
5.41: “But if he is afraid, and encamps beyond the river, we shall go over to him, and overcome him.”
5.42: Now when Yahuḏah came near the wadi, he made the scribes of the people remain by the wadi, to whom he gave command saying, “Allow no man to remain in the camp, but let all come to the battle.”
5.43: So he went over to them first, and all the people after him. Then all the gentiles being defeated before him, threw away their weapons and fled to the temple that was at Qarnayim.
5.44: But they took the city and burned the temple with all that were in it. Thus Qarnayim was subdued, neither could they stand any longer before Yahuḏah.
5.45: Then Yahuḏah gathered together all the Yisra’ĕlites that were in the country of Gil’aḏ, from the least to the greatest, even their wives and their children and their goods - a very great company - so that they might come to the land of Yahuḏah.
5.46: Now when they came to Ephron, - this was a great city in the way they were going; very well fortified - they could not turn from it, either to the right hand or the left, but had to pass through the midst of it.
5.47: Then those of the city shut them out, and stopped up the gates with stones.
5.48: So Yahuḏah sent to them in a peaceable manner saying, “Let us pass through your land to go to our own country and none shall do you any harm. We will only pass through on foot.” However, they would not open to him.
5.49: Therefore Yahuḏah called a command to be made throughout the army, that every man should pitch his tent in the place where he was.
5.50: So the soldiers encamped, and attacked the city all that day and all that night, till in the end the city was delivered into his hands;
5.51: who then slew all the males with the edge of the sword and tore down the city and took the spoil from there, and passed through the city over those that were slain.
5.52: After this, went they over the Yardĕn into the great plain before Bĕyth She’an.
5.53: And Yahuḏah gathered together those that came behind and encouraged the people all the way through till they came to the land of Yahuḏah.
5.54: So they went up to Mount Tsiyon with joy and gladness, where they offered burnt offerings - because not one of them were slain - until they had returned in peace.
5.55: Now during the time Yahuḏah and Yahonathan were in the land of Gil’aḏ and Shim’on his brother in Galil before Ptolemais,
5.56: Yosĕph the son of Zeḵaryah and Azaryah, captains of the garrisons, heard of the brave acts and mighty deeds which they had done.
5.57: So they said, “Let us also get ourselves a name, and go fight against the gentiles that are round about us.”
5.58: So when they had given charge to the garrison that was with them, they went toward Yaḇneh.
5.59: Then Gorgias and his men came out of the city to fight against them.
5.60: And so it was, that Yosĕph and Azaryah were put to flight, and pursued to the borders of Yahuḏah, and about two thousand men of the people of Yisra’ĕl were slain that day.
5.61: So there was a great overthrow among the children of Yisra’ĕl, because they were not obedient to Yahuḏah and his brothers, but thought to do some mighty deed.
5.62: But these men did not come from the seed of those by whose hand deliverance was given to Yisra’ĕl.
5.63: However, the man Yahuḏah and his brothers were greatly renowned in the sight of all Yisra’ĕl and of all the gentiles wherever their name was heard of;
5.64: so that the people assembled to them with joyful cheers.
5.65: Afterward Yahuḏah went out with his brothers and fought against the children of Ĕsaw in the land toward the south, where he smote Ḥeḇron and its towns and pulled down its fortress and burned the towers round about.
5.66: From there he moved to go to the land of the Pelishtites and passed through Shomeron.
5.67: At that time some kohenim, wanting to show their courage, were slain in battle, for they went out to fight recklessly.
5.68: So Yahuḏah turned to Ashdoḏ in the land of the Pelishtites, and when he had pulled down their altars and burned their carved images with fire and plundered their cities, he returned to the land of Yahuḏah.

6.1: About that time meleḵ Antioḵos travelling through the high countries heard it said that Elumais in the country of Paras was a city greatly renowned for riches, silver and gold;
6.2: and that there was a very rich temple in it in which were coverings of gold and breastplates and shields which Alexandros, son of Philippos the Makedonian meleḵ, who reigned first among the Yawanites, had left there.
6.3: Therefore he came and sought to take the city, and to plunder it; but he was not able, because those of the city having had warning,
6.4: rose up against him in battle. So he fled and departed from there in great distress, and returned to Baḇel.
6.5: And there came one who brought him news of Paras, that the armies, which went against the land of Yahuḏah, were put to flight,
6.6: and that Lusias, who went out first with great strength was driven away by the Yahuḏim; and that they were strengthened by the armor and strength and store of plunder, which they had taken from the armies whom they had destroyed.
6.7: Also, that they had pulled down the abomination, which he had placed upon the altar in Yerushalayim, and that they had surrounded the Miqdash with high walls as before, and its city Bĕyth Tsur.
6.8: Now when the meleḵ heard these words, he was astonished and distressed, so he laid himself down on his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not resulted as he planned.
6.9: And there he stayed many days, for his grief increased further, and he thought that he would die.
6.10: So he called for all his friends, and said to them, “The sleep is gone from my eyes, and my heart fails for every concern.
6.11: “And I thought within myself, ‘Into what tribulation have I come, and how great a flood of misery it is, in which I now am!’ for I was respectable and well loved in my power.
6.12: “But now I remember the evils that I did at Yerushalayim, and that I took all the vessels of gold and silver that were there, and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Yahuḏah without reason.
6.13: “I perceive therefore, that for this reason these troubles have come upon me, and, see, I perish through great grief in a strange land.”
6.14: Then he called for Philippos, one of his friends, who he made ruler over all his reign,
6.15: and gave him the crown, and his robe, and his seal, so that he should bring up his son Antioḵos, and raise him up for the reign.
6.16: So meleḵ Antioḵos died there in the hundred and forty-ninth year.
6.17: Now when Lusias knew that the meleḵ was dead, he appointed Antioḵos his son, whom he had brought up from youth to reign in his place, and his name he called Eupator.
6.18: About this time those that were in the fortress enclosed the Yisra’ĕlites round about the Miqdash, and continually sought their evil, and the strengthening of the gentiles.
6.19: Therefore Yahuḏah, intending to destroy them, called all the people together to besiege them.
6.20: So they came together, and besieged them in the hundred and fiftieth year, and he made mounts for shot against them, and other engines.
6.21: However some of those that were besieged escaped, to whom some wicked men of Yisra’ĕl joined themselves.
6.22: And they went to the meleḵ, and said, “How long will it be till you execute judgment, and avenge our brothers?
6.23: “We have been willing to serve your father, and do as he would have us, and to obey his commands.
6.24: “For this reason those of our nation besiege the fortress, and are alienated from us! And as many of us as they could fall upon, they slew, and plundered our inheritance.
6.25: “Neither have they stretched out their hand against us alone, but also against their borders.
6.26: “And, see, this day they are besieging the fortress at Yerushalayim, to take it; the Miqdash also, and they have fortified Bĕyth Tsur.
6.27: “Therefore if you do not prevent them quickly, they will do greater matters than these, neither shall you be able to rule them.”
6.28: Now when the meleḵ heard this, he was wroth, and gathered together all his associates and the captains of his army, and those that had charge of the horses.
6.29: There also came to him bands of hired soldiers from other reigns, and from islands of the sea,
6.30: so that the number of his army was a hundred thousand footmen, and twenty thousand horsemen, and thirty-two elephants trained for battle.
6.31: These went through Eḏom, and encamped against Bĕyth Tsur, which they assaulted many days, making engines of battle. But those of Bĕyth Tsur came out, and burned them with fire, and fought bravely.
6.32: After this, Yahuḏah moved from the fortress, and encamped in Bĕyth Zeḵaryah, opposite the meleḵ’s camp.
6.33: Then the meleḵ rising very early, marched fiercely with his army toward Bĕyth Zeḵaryah, where his armies prepared for battle, and sounded the trumpets.
6.34: And so, that they might provoke the elephants to fight, they showed them the blood of grapes and mulberries.
6.35: And they divided the beasts among the armies, and for every elephant they appointed one thousand men, armed with coats of mail, and with bronze helmets on their heads. And besides this, for every beast were assigned five hundred of the best horsemen.
6.36: These were ready at every occasion. Wherever the beast was, and wherever the beast went, they went also, neither did they depart from it.
6.37: And upon the beasts there were strong wooden towers, which covered every one of them, and were girded tightly to them with devices. There were also, thirty-two strong men on every one that fought upon them, besides the Hodite that directed it.
6.38: As for the remainder of the horsemen, they positioned them on this side and that side of the two divisions of the army giving them signals what to do, and being armed all over among the ranks.
6.39: Now when the sun shone upon the shields of gold and bronze, the mountains glistened, and shone like lamps of fire.
6.40: So part of the meleḵ’s army being spread over the high mountains, and part on the valleys below, marched on boldly and in formation.
6.41: Therefore all that heard the noise of their multitude, and the marching of the army, and the rattling of the armor, were moved; for the army was very great and mighty.
6.42: Then Yahuḏah and his army drew near, and joined in battle, and six hundred men of the meleḵ’s army were slain.
6.43: Eli’ezer, also named Savaran, perceiving that one of the beasts armed with royal armor, was higher than all the rest, and supposing that the meleḵ was upon him,
6.44: put himself in danger, so that he might deliver his people, and obtain a lasting name for himself.
6.45: Therefore he ran upon him courageously through the midst of the battle, slaying on the right hand and on the left, so that they were divided from him on both sides.
6.46: Having done so, he crept under the elephant, and thrust it underneath, and slew it, so the elephant fell down upon him, and he died there.
6.47: However the rest of the Yahuḏim, seeing the strength of the meleḵ, and the violence of his forces, turned away from them.
6.48: Then the meleḵ’s army went up to Yerushalayim to meet them, and the meleḵ pitched his tents against Yahuḏah, and against Mount Tsiyon.
6.49: But he made peace with those that were in Bĕyth Tsur; for they came out of the city, because they had no food there to endure the siege, being a year of rest for the land.
6.50: So the meleḵ took Bĕyth Tsur, and appointed a garrison there to guard it.
6.51: As for the Miqdash, he besieged it many days, and appointed siege engines there with weapons and instruments to throw fire and stones, and catapults and weapons to shoot arrows.
6.52: So they also made engines against their engines, and withheld them in battle a long time.
6.53: Yet in the end, their containers being without food - for it was the seventh year, and those in Yahuḏah that were delivered from the gentiles had eaten up the remains of the store.
6.54: So there were only a few left in the Miqdash, and because the scarcity of food prevailed against them, they were compelled to disperse themselves, every man to his own place.
6.55: At that time Lusias heard it said, that Philippos - whom Antioḵos the meleḵ, while he lived - had appointed to bring up his son Antioḵos to be meleḵ;
6.56: had returned from Paras and Maḏai, and the meleḵ’s army that also went with him, and that he planned to seize the control of affairs for himself.
6.57: Therefore he went in haste, and said to the meleḵ and the captains of the army and the company, “We diminish daily, and our food runs short, and the place we lay siege to is strong, and the affairs of the reign lie upon us.
6.58: “Now therefore let us be friends with these men, and make peace with them, and with all their nation;
6.59: and make a covenant with them, that they shall live after their Laws, as they did before. For they are displeased because we abolished their Laws, and therefore, have done all these matters.”
6.60: So the meleḵ and the princes were pleased; therefore he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted.
6.61: The meleḵ and the princes also made an oath to them, so they went out of the stronghold.
6.62: Then the meleḵ entered into Mount Tsiyon; but when he saw the strength of the place, he broke his oath that he had made, and gave command to pull down the wall round about.
6.63: Afterward he departed in haste, and returned to Antioḵeia, where he found Philippos to be master of the city. So he fought against him, and took the city by force.

7.1: In the one hundred and fiftieth year, Dĕmĕtrios the son of Seleukus departed from Rome, and came up with a few men to a city of the sea coast, and reigned there.
7.2: And as he entered into the palace of his ancestors, it had come to pass, that his army had taken Antioḵos and Lusias, to bring them to him.
7.3: Therefore, when he knew it, he said, “Do not let me see their faces.”
7.4: So his army slew them. Now when Dĕmĕtrios was appointed to the throne of his reign,
7.5: there came to him all the wicked and evil men of Yisra’ĕl, having Elyaqim, who desired to be kohĕn ha’gadol, as their captain.
7.6: And they accused the people before the meleḵ, saying, “Yahuḏah and his brothers have slain all your friends, and driven us out of our own land.
7.7: “Now therefore, send some man whom you trust, and let him go and see what disorder he has made among us, and in the meleḵ’s land, and let him punish them with all those that assist them.”
7.8: Then the meleḵ chose Bakḵidĕs, a friend of the meleḵ, who ruled beyond the River, and was a great man in the reign, and trustworthy to the meleḵ,
7.9: and he sent him with the wicked Elyaqim, whom he made kohĕn ha’gadol, and commanded that he should take vengeance on the children of Yisra’ĕl.
7.10: So they departed, and came with a large force into the land of Yahuḏah, where they sent messengers to Yahuḏah and his brothers with peaceable words, deceitfully.
7.11: But they gave no heed to their words, for they saw that they had come with a large force.
7.12: Then a company of scribes gathered to Elyaqim and Bakḵidĕs, to require right-ruling.
7.13: Now the Ḥasiḏim were the first among the children of Yisra’ĕl that sought peace from them,
7.14: for they said, “One that is a kohĕn of the seed of Aharon has come with this army, and he will do us no wrong.”
7.15: So he spoke to them peaceably, and swore to them, saying, “We will neither do evil to you nor your friends.”
7.16: So they believed him; however he took from them sixty men, and slew them in one day, to fill the words which are written:
7.17: “The flesh of your qodeshim they have thrown out, and their blood they have shed round about Yerushalayim, with no one to bury them.”
7.18: Therefore the fear and dread of them fell upon all the people, who said, “There is neither truth nor righteousness in them; for they have broken the covenant and oath that they made.”
7.19: After this, Bakḵidĕs moved from Yerushalayim, and pitched his tents in Bĕyth Zatha, where he sent and took many of the men that had forsaken him, and some of the people also, and when he had slain them, he threw them into a large pit.
7.20: Then he entrusted the land to Elyaqim, and left with him a force to assist him; so Bakḵidĕs returned to the meleḵ.
7.21: But Elyaqim contended to be kohĕn ha’gadol.
7.22: And all those who troubled the people assembled to him, who, after they had taken the land of Yahuḏah into their power, did much evil in Yisra’ĕl.
7.23: Now when Yahuḏah saw all the evil that Elyaqim and his company had done among the Yisra’ĕlites, even more than the gentiles,
7.24: he went out to all the coastlands of Yahuḏah round about, and took vengeance on those that had revolted from him, so that they no longer dared go out into the country.
7.25: On the other side, when Elyaqim saw that Yahuḏah and his army had gotten the upper hand, and knew that he was not able to withstand their strength, he went again to the meleḵ, and said all the worst about them that he could.
7.26: Then the meleḵ sent Nikanor, one of his honorable princes, a man that bore deadly hatred for Yisra’ĕl, with a command to destroy the people.
7.27: So Nikanor came to Yerushalayim with a large force, and sent to Yahuḏah and his brothers deceitfully with friendly words, saying,
7.28: “Let there be no battle between me and you. I will come with a few men, that I may see you in peace.”
7.29: Therefore he came to Yahuḏah, and they greeted one another peaceably; however the enemies were prepared to take away Yahuḏah with violence.
7.30: After this matter was known to Yahuḏah, to know that he came to him with deceit, he was very afraid of him, and would no longer see his face.
7.31: Also, when Nikanor saw that his plan was discovered, went out to fight against Yahuḏah beside Kephar Salem,
7.32: where about five thousand men were slain from Nikanor’s side, and the rest fled to the city of Dawiḏ.
7.33: After this went Nikanor up to Mount Tsiyon, and some of the kohenim and some of the elders of the people came out of the Miqdash, to greet him peaceably, and to show him the burnt offering that was offered for the meleḵ.
7.34: But he mocked them, and laughed at them, and abused them shamefully, and spoke proudly,
7.35: and swore in his wrath, saying, “Unless Yahuḏah and his army are now delivered into my hands, if I ever come again in safety, I will burn up this House!” and with that he went out in a great rage.
7.36: Then the kohenim entered in, and stood before the altar and the Hĕyḵal weeping, and saying,
7.37: “You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, chose this House to be called by Your Name, and to be a House of prayer and petition for Your people.
7.38: “Be avenged on this man and his army, and let them fall by the sword. Remember their blasphemies, and do not allow them to continue any longer.”
7.39: So Nikanor went out of Yerushalayim, and pitched his tents in Bĕyth Ḥoron, where an army out of Suria met him.
7.40: But Yahuḏah pitched in Ḥaḏashah with three thousand men, and he prayed there saying,
7.41: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, when those that were sent from the meleḵ of Ashshur blasphemed, Your messenger went out, and smote a hundred and eighty-five thousand of them.
7.42: “In the same way, destroy this army before us today, that the rest may know that he has spoken blasphemy against Your Miqdash, and judge him according to his wickedness.”
7.43: So on the thirteenth day of the month Aḏar the armies joined in battle, but Nikanor’s army was defeated, and he himself was the first slain in the battle.
7.44: Now when Nikanor’s army saw that he was slain, they threw down their weapons, and fled.
7.45: Then they pursued after them a day’s journey, from Ḥaḏashah to Gezer, sounding a shout after them with their trumpets.
7.46: So they came out from all of the towns of Yahuḏah round about and closed them in, so that they, turning back upon those that pursued them, were all slain with the sword, and not one of them was left.
7.47: Afterward they took the spoils, and the plunder, and smote off Nikanor’s head, and his right hand, which he stretched out so proudly, and took them away, and hanged them up toward Yerushalayim.
7.48: Because of this the people rejoiced greatly, and they kept that day as a day of great gladness.
7.49: And they ordained to guard this day yearly, being the thirteenth of Aḏar.
7.50: Thus the land of Yahuḏah was at rest a little while.

8.1: Now Yahuḏah had heard of the Romans, that they were brave and mighty men, and such that would kindly accept all that joined themselves to them, and make a covenant of peace with all that came to them;
8.2: and that they were men of great courage. To him was also told of their battles and notable deeds which they had done among the Galatians, and how they had conquered them, and brought them under tribute;
8.3: and what they had done in the country of Spania, in taking the mines of silver and gold which is there;
8.4: and that by their strategy and patience they had conquered all that place, though it was very far from them; and of the melaḵim that also came against them from the ends of the earth, till they had defeated them, and given them a great overthrow, so that the rest gave them tribute every year.
8.5: Besides this, how they had defeated Philippos and Perseus, meleḵ of the Ḥittites in battle, with others that lifted themselves up against them and had overcome them.
8.6: Also how Antioḵos the great meleḵ of Asia, that came against them in battle, having a hundred and twenty elephants with horsemen and chariots, and a very great army, was defeated by them;
8.7: and how they took him alive, and made a covenant that he and those that reigned after him should pay a great tribute and give hostages, and that which was agreed upon.
8.8: And the country of Hodu, and Maḏai and Ludia and of the best lands which they took from him and gave to Meleḵ Eumĕnĕs.
8.9: And how the Yawanites had determined to come and destroy them;
8.10: and that they, having knowledge of this sent against them a certain captain, and fighting with them slew many of them, and took away captive their wives and their children, and plundered them, and took possession of their lands, and pulled down their strongholds, and took them to be their servants to this day.
8.11: It was also told him, how they destroyed and brought under their rule all other reigns and islands that at any time resisted them,
8.12: but they kept peace with their friends and those that relied upon them; and that they had conquered reigns both far and near, so that all that heard of their name were afraid of them.
8.13: Also that whom they would assist to reign, those reigned; and again, whom they determined, they displaced. Lastly, that they were greatly exalted,
8.14: yet for all this, none of them wore a crown or was clothed in purple, to be made great by it.
8.15: And, how they had made for themselves a senate house, in which three hundred and twenty men sat in council daily, consulting always for the people, so that they might be well ordered;
8.16: and that they committed their government to one man every year, who ruled over all their country, and that all were obedient to that one, and that there was neither envy nor strife among them.
8.17: In consideration of these matters, Yahuḏah chose Eupolemus the son of Yoḥanan, the son of Haqqots, and Yason the son of Eli’ezer, and sent them to Rome, to make a covenant of peace and ally with them,
8.18: and to ask them that they would take the yoke from them; for they saw that the reign of the Yawanites oppressed Yisra’ĕl with bondage.
8.19: So they went to Rome, which was a very great journey, and came into the senate, where they spoke and said,
8.20: “Yahuḏah Maqqaḇah with his brothers, and the people of the Yahuḏim, have sent us to you, to make peace and an alliance with you, and that we might be counted your allies and friends.”
8.21: So that matter pleased the Romans well.
8.22: And this is the copy of the letter which the senate wrote back again on tablets of bronze, and sent to Yerushalayim, that they would possess a memorial of peace and alliance for them there:
8.23: “Good success be to the Romans, and to the people of the Yahuḏim, by sea and by land forever. Also the sword and enemy be far from them.
8.24: “If there should come first any battle upon the Romans or any of their allies throughout all their reign,
8.25: the people of the Yahuḏim shall assist them at the appointed time with all their heart.
8.26: “Neither shall they give whatever to those that fight against them, or aid them with food, weapons, silver, or ships, as it seems good to the Romans; but they shall guard their covenants without taking any for this.
8.27: “Also in the same manner, if battle should come first upon the nation of the Yahuḏim, the Romans shall assist them with all their heart, according to the time appointed for them.
8.28: “Neither shall food be given to those that take part against them, or weapons, or silver, or ships, as it seems good to the Romans; but they shall guard their covenants, and that, without deceit.
8.29: “According to these articles, the Romans make a covenant with the people of the Yahuḏim.
8.30: “However, if after this, the one party or the other shall think by rights to add or diminish whatever, they may do so at their pleasure, and whatever they shall add or take away shall be consented to.
8.31: “And regarding the evils that Dĕmĕtrios has done to the Yahuḏim, we have written to him, saying, ‘Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends and allies the Yahuḏim?
8.32: ‘If therefore they complain against you any more, we will do right by them, and fight with you by sea and by land.’ ”

9.1: Furthermore, when Dĕmĕtrios heard that Nikanor and his army were slain in battle, he sent Bakḵidĕs and Elyaqim to the land of Yahuḏah a second time, and with them the main force of his army,
9.2: who went out by the way that leads to Gilgal, and pitched their tents before Mĕsaloth, which is in Arbela. And after they had won it, they slew much people.
9.3: Also, on the first month of the hundred and fifty-second year, they encamped before Yerushalayim.
9.4: From there they moved, and went to Beroia, with twenty thousand footmen and two thousand horsemen.
9.5: Now Yahuḏah had pitched his tents at El’asah, with three thousand chosen men with him,
9.6: who, seeing the multitude of the mighty army opposing him, was greatly afraid. Therefore many withdrew from the army, so that no more than eight hundred men of them stayed.
9.7: Therefore when Yahuḏah saw that his army slipped away, and that the battle pressed upon him, he was greatly troubled in mind and very distressed, for he had no time to assemble them together.
9.8: Nevertheless, to those that remained he said, “Let us arise and go up against our enemies, if possible we are able to defeat them.”
9.9: But they pleaded with him saying, “We shall never be able! Let us now rather save our lives, and afterward we will return with our brothers, and fight against them, for we are but a few.”
9.10: Then Yahuḏah said, “Elohim forbid that I should do this matter, and flee away from them. If our time has come, let us die bravely for our brothers, and let us not stain our honor.”
9.11: With that, the army of Bakḵidĕs moved out of their tents, and stood opposite them; their horsemen being divided into two companies, and their slingers and archers going before the army. And those that marched in the front were all mighty men.
9.12: As for Bakḵidĕs, he was in the right wing. So the army drew near to the two divisions, and sounded their trumpets.
9.13: Those of Yahuḏah’s side, even they also sounded their trumpets, so that the earth shook at the noise of the armies, and the battle continued from morning till night.
9.14: Now when Yahuḏah perceived that Bakḵidĕs and the strength of his army were on the right side, he took with him all the brave men,
9.15: who defeated the right wing, and pursued them to Mount Ashdoḏ.
9.16: But when those on the left wing saw that those on the right wing were defeated, they pursued Yahuḏah, and those that were with him hard at the heels from behind.
9.17: Therefore there was a great battle, so that many were slain on both sides.
9.18: Yahuḏah was also killed, and the remnant fled.
9.19: Then Yahonathan and Shim’on took Yahuḏah their brother, and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modi’im.
9.20: And they mourned him, and all Yisra’ĕl made a great lamentation for him, and mourned many days, saying,
9.21: “How the brave man has fallen that delivered Yisra’ĕl!”
9.22: As for the other matters concerning Yahuḏah and his battles, and the mighty deeds which he did, and his greatness, are they not written; for they were very many.
9.23: Now after the death of Yahuḏah, the wicked began to lift their heads in all the coasts of Yisra’ĕl, and there arose all those doing wickedness.
9.24: In those days there was also a very great scarcity of food; the land revolted because of this, and went with them.
9.25: Then Bakḵidĕs chose these wicked men, and made them masters of the land.
9.26: And they made inquiry and sought for Yahuḏah’s friends, and brought them to Bakḵidĕs, who took vengeance on them, and mistreated them.
9.27: So was there a great affliction in Yisra’ĕl, the like of which was not seen, since the time that a naḇi was among them.
9.28: Because of this, all Yahuḏah’s companions came together, and said to Yahonathan,
9.29: “Since your brother Yahuḏah died, we have no man like him to go out against our enemies, and Bakḵidĕs, and against those of our nation that are adversaries to us.
9.30: “Now therefore, we have chosen you today to be our leader and captain in his place, that you may fight our battles.”
9.31: Therefore, at that time Yahonathan took the authority upon himself, and rose up instead of his brother Yahuḏah.
9.32: But when Bakḵidĕs learned of this, he sought to slay him.
9.33: Then Yahonathan, and Shim’on his brother, and all that were with him, perceiving this, fled into the wilderness of Teqowa, and pitched their tents by the water of the pool Asphar.
9.34: When Bakḵidĕs knew, he came near to the Yardĕn with all his army on the Shabbath day.
9.35: Now Yahonathan had sent his brother Yoḥanan, a captain of the people, to ask his friends the Naḇothites, that they might leave with them their goods, which was much.
9.36: But the children of Yambri came out of Mĕyḏeḇa, and took Yoḥanan, and all that he had, and went their way with it.
9.37: After this, word came to Yahonathan and Shim’on his brother, that the children of Yambri held a great marriage, and were bringing the bride, the daughter of one of the great princes of Kena’an from Naḏaḇath, with a great procession.
9.38: Therefore they remembered Yoḥanan their brother, and went up, and hid themselves under cover of the mountain,
9.39: where they lifted up their eyes, and looked, and, see, there was a great tumult and a great procession. And the bridegroom came out, and his friends and brothers, to meet them with tambourines and music and many instruments.
9.40: Then Yahonathan and those that were with him rose up against them from the place where they lay in ambush, and made a slaughter of them, so that many fell down dead, and the remnant fled into the mountain; and they took all their spoil.
9.41: Thus the marriage was turned into mourning, and the noise of their song into lamentation.
9.42: So when they had fully avenged the blood of their brother, they turned again to the wadi of the Yardĕn.
9.43: Now when Bakḵidĕs heard of this, he came on the Shabbath day to the banks of the Yardĕn with a great force.
9.44: Then Yahonathan said to his army, “Let us go up now and fight for our lives, for it does not stand with us today, as in time past.
9.45: “For, see, the battle is before us and behind us, and the water of the Yardĕn on this side and that side, the wadi and also the forest, neither is there a place for us to turn aside.
9.46: “Therefore cry out now to the shamayim, that you may be delivered from the hand of your enemies.”
9.47: Therefore, they joined battle, and Yahonathan stretched out his hand to smite Bakḵidĕs, but he turned back from him.
9.48: Then Yahonathan and those that were with him leaped into the Yardĕn, and swam over to the other bank; however, the others did not pass over the Yardĕn to them.
9.49: So about one thousand men of Bakḵidĕs’ army were slain that day.
9.50: Afterward Bakḵidĕs returned to Yerushalayim and repaired the strong cites in Yahuḏah, the fort in Yeriḥo and Amma’us and Bĕyth Ḥoron and Bĕyth Ĕl and Timnathah, Pirathon and Tsaphon. He strengthened these with high walls, with gates and with bars.
9.51: And he appointed a garrison in them, that they might do evil to Yisra’ĕl.
9.52: He also fortified the city of Bĕyth Tsur, and Gezer, and the tower, and put forces in them, and provisions of food.
9.53: He also took the chief men’s sons in the land for hostages, and put them into the tower at Yerushalayim to be guarded.
9.54: And in the hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Elyaqim commanded that the wall of the inner court of the Miqdash should be pulled down. He also pulled down the works of the neḇi’im.
9.55: And as he began to pull down, even at that time Elyaqim was plagued, and his works were hindered; for his mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, so that he could no longer speak a word, nor give orders concerning his house.
9.56: So Elyaqim died at that time in great torment.
9.57: Now when Bakḵidĕs saw that Elyaqim was dead, he returned to the meleḵ. So the land of Yahuḏah was at rest two years.
9.58: Then all the wicked men held a council, saying, “See, Yahonathan and his company are at ease, and dwell without concern. Now therefore we will bring Bakḵidĕs here, who shall take them all in one night.”
9.59: So they went and consulted with him.
9.60: Then he moved, and came with a great army, and sent letters secretly to his supporters in Yahuḏah, that they should take Yahonathan and those that were with him. However they could not, because their counsel was known to them.
9.61: Therefore they took the men of the land that were the cause of that evil - about fifty people - and slew them.
9.62: Afterward Yahonathan, and Shim’on, and those that were with him, escaped to Bĕyth Bĕsai, which is in the wilderness, and they repaired the ruins there, and strengthened it.
9.63: When Bakḵidĕs knew this, he gathered together all his army, and sent word to those that were of Yahuḏah.
9.64: Then he went and laid siege against Bĕyth Bĕsai. And they fought against it for a long time and built siege engines.
9.65: But Yahonathan left his brother Shim’on in the city, and went out himself into the land, and with a certain number he went out.
9.66: And he smote Odomera and his brothers, and the children of Phaseiron in their tent.
9.67: And when he began to smite them, and came up with his forces, Shim’on and his army went out of the city, and burned the siege engines,
9.68: and fought against Bakḵidĕs, who was defeated by them. And they distressed him greatly, for his counsel and hardship was worthless.
9.69: Therefore he was very wroth at the wicked men that gave him counsel to come into the land, so he slew many of them, and intended to return to his own land.
9.70: When Yahonathan knew of this, he sent ambassadors to him, so that he should make peace with him, and deliver them the prisoners;
9.71: which he accepted, and did according to his demands, and swore to him that he would never do him harm all the days of his life.
9.72: Therefore when he had restored the prisoners to him that he had taken previously out of the land of Yahuḏah, he returned and went his way to his own land, neither did he come to their borders any more.
9.73: Thus the sword ceased from Yisra’ĕl, and Yahonathan dwelt at Miḵmas, and began to rule the people, and he destroyed the wicked men out of Yisra’ĕl.
